I just polished off The Deadly Tower of Monsters.  The premise is simple:  You are watching a VHS of an old low budget 50s pulp sci-fi B movie while the director records the commentary for the DVD release.    You control the characters (leading man, space woman who has never seen a man, robot) through a sort of 3D action-shooter-platformer, complete with VHS video artifacts, cheesy sci-fi soundtrack, and the director commenting on the actors, the filming, and the oddities that don't make any sense (like how player deaths were just footage accidentally left in, or how much the prop guy hated having to re-build all of the crates that got smashed.)  The gameplay was fun, challenging at times, but not really tough on normal difficulty.  There were optional collectibles, weapon upgrades, basics skills, and special abilities.  The story has you climbing a massive, massive tower that goes from ground level to orbit, and at any point you can look down and see the entire thing, or even jump off and fall all the way down to any point you'd been at previously, landing with your trusty jetpack at the last second (and you could always teleport back.)  They pull off the B movie schtick brilliantly.   The VHS effects really work, and the look is spot-on.  The 'monsters' you fight are obviously guys stuck in a rubber suit, and if anything flies you can clearly see the wires.  When larger monsters appear, they're animated in such a way that they look like the were filmed using stop-motion photography.  You carried two melee and two ranged weapons from a large selection, all typical fun sci-fi nonsense (including one blaster that was obviously an electric razor, and one gun that was a small vacuum.)  My only real complaints were that the last chapter's narrative kind of went off the tracks, and that some of the special abilities were never really communicated to the player (I still don't know exactly what the big bubble thing that everyone had actually did.)  It was a little too easy at times, but again, I played on normal.  It was still tough enough that boss fights required some effort, but never to the point of being dull or frustrating.  It was the perfect length for that, too, being maybe 4-5 hours.  Any longer and it would have gotten tedious, but it was fine for that length of time.  Not a perfect game, but a ton of fun and a great setting.  Maybe a 7.5/10.

Even though Rust is still in early alpha stages with only a couple in-game items it still provides plenty of entertainment that can only get better as more items and features are implemented and the map is expanded.    Unlike other FPS games where you have scary or stressful moments and know you can relax right after, Rust provides a constant level of terror for every sound you hear. There is no relaxing in this game. Even logging out gives no respite as your character simply goes to sleep at the last location you were standing. This means no avoiding a fight by simply closing the game. Your body will simply slump to the floor and be easy pickings for wildlife and other players.    Yes, other players... trust is a tricky thing in Rust. You never know the intentions of anyone else in the game. Resources are scarce and people will kill for them. That plane flying over dropping supplies? It's both a blessing and a curse. You know there are going to be rare items and food parcels in those drops. Unfortunately, so does everyone else who saw it fly over. They might share the spoils with you and then suddenly they find a shotgun in the last crate. Suddenly they don't seem to feel like you deserve half the food.    Human nature is a tricksie hobbitses, welcome to Rust.
The only downside to this game is that it's the only one likely to ever be ported to PC! Bring us the rest of them, already!

Matriarchs, virtually unhittable and resistant to most anything. again you will muddle through as you tech up some more and brute force your way through them when encountered. UE4で造りなおしたアクアノックス。 続編でもリメイクでもない新作であり、リブート的なタイトルが付いているがおそらく続編は出ない。  このゲームの問題点は「パイロット視点で潜水艇に乗って戦うゲーム」なのに、それを活かせていない点にある。 三次元的なマップを三次元的に移動できるという点はよいのだが、問題は敵との戦闘だ。 先に見つけて奇襲するだとか、着底させてやり過ごすだとか、機動力に勝る艦で背後をとって一方的にボコるみたいなおもしろそうな事は一切できない。 ゲームがうまい下手に関係なく、妙に命中精度の高い敵と正面から撃ちあい、シールドが破れたらやられる前に張りなおすというゲームになりがちだ。戦闘の攻略も「上手に避けながら攻撃する」のではなく、地形を壁として使い、一度に撃ちあう敵の数を制限するみたいなしょうもないものになりやすい。  また、キャラやストーリーにも引き込まれる要素が一切ないのも深刻だ。 UIに比べると会話の和訳は割とまともなのだが、かなり強引な導入なので感情移入できる奴は居ないだろう。 何なら主人公＝プレイヤーが誰かなのかすら分からないまである。  射撃で戦うRPGとしては完成しており、値段も安価で日本語対応済みなのでおススメにはするが、これは「買おうと思っていた人を翻意させるほどではない」という意味で、何でもいいから何かおもしろいゲームを探しているという人に「これを選べ」という意味ではない。

[h1]มันคือ Bannished ฉบับย่อส่วนที่มีกลิ่นไอแบบ Wild West[/h1]  โดยพื้นฐานแล้ว [i]Depraved[/i] ก็คือ [i]Banished[/i] เวอร์ชั่น Wild West หรือเกมสร้างหมู่บ้านในสไตล์คาวบอยตะวันตกที่มีระบบการจัดการสินค้าและทรัพยากรทั่วไปความคล้ายคลึงกัน แต่เกมนี้อาจจะมีรายละเอียดที่ไม่ลึกเท่าและมีกลิ่นไอของความเป็น City Builder/Survival เพียงเล็กน้อย อย่างไรก็ดีถ้าคุณชอบเกมแนวสร้างหมู่บ้าน เมืองเล็กๆ หรืออาณานิคม [i]Depraved[/i]  ก็เป็นตัวเลือกที่ดีเกมนึงซึ่งราคาไม่ได้แพงอะไร และน่าจะช่วยมอบบรรยากาศใหม่ๆ ในการเล่นเกมสร้างเมืองได้เป็นอย่างดีด้วย  เกมเพลย์หลักคือการสร้างเมืองสไตล์คาวบอยอย่างที่กล่าวไปนั่นแหละ ไม่มีเนื้อเรื่อง ไม่มีภารกิจอะไร เริ่มมามีโหมดเดียวให้คุณได้เลือกเล่น คุณสามารถปรับระดับความยาก ความก้าวร้าวของสัตว์ป่า และเลือกสุ่มสร้างแผนที่ได้ คุณจะเริ่มต้นด้วยรถคาราวาน 1 คันที่สามารถเอาไปสร้างเป็น Town Hall ตรงไหนก็ได้บนแผนที่ จากนั้นก็ขยับขยายสร้างหมู่บ้านกันต่อไป สร้างโรงตัดไม้ บ้านคนงาน โรงม้า สถานีพยาบาล และขยับขยายสร้างสถานีรถไฟเพื่อค้าขายทำเควสต่อไป (สำหรับถนนนั้นจะเกิดขึ้นเองตามไลน์ที่ชาวบ้านเดินไปมา) ตัวเกมไม่มีเป้าหมายแน่ชัด คือคุณต้องเล่นมันไปเรื่อยๆ ปลดล็อกสิ่งก่อสร้างต่างๆ ตามเงื่อนไข ซึ่งสุดท้ายมันอาจจะให้ความรู้สึกเป็นเส้นตรงเกินไปนิด แต่สำหรับความท้าทายในเกมก็ถือว่าอยู่ในขั้นน่าสนใจ เกมมีลูกเล่นอย่างการจ้าง NPC นักแม่นปืนเข้ามาประจำเมือง มีเรื่องการจับคนร้ายที่ติดค่าหัวสไตล์ Wild west เพื่อนำไปขึ้นรางวัลสร้างรายได้  บทสอนและขั้นตอนการเล่นในเกมไม่ได้บอกอะไรละเอียดนัก แต่คุณก็สามารถงมหาได้เองง่ายๆ เพราะเกมไม่ซับซ้อนอะไร การขยายหมู่บ้านทำได้โดยการซื้อพื้นที่ด้วยเงิน และพยายามสร้างที่อยู่อาศัยเพิ่มเพื่อดึงดูดประชากรเข้ามา ประชากรก็จะมีระดับแตกต่างกันซึ่งจำเป็นในการพัฒนาเมืองในด้านต่างๆ ตามไปด้วยครับ  [b]Note[/b] **เกมเพลย์หลักช่วง Early Access กับตัวเต็มไม่ได้แตกต่างกันมากนัก สิ่งที่แตกต่างคือการขัดเกลาและเก็บรายละเอียดในระบบ รวมถึงการปรับปรุงกราฟิกให้ดูดีกว่าเดิม  สำหรับปัญหาทั่วไปและ Performance ในเกมตัวเต็มนั้น ต้องบอกว่าผมไม่เจออาการค้างหรือเกมล่มเหมือนที่คนเล่นอื่นเจอแต่ประการใด (ช่วง Early Access นั้นมีบ้างนิดหน่อย) ถือว่าทีมงานปรับปรุงมันออกมาได้ค่อนข้างดี แต่ความสมดุลในส่วน Progression ยังคงมีให้เห็นอยู่ (ยกตัวอย่างคือ ชาวบ้านเกิดบาดเจ็บ หรือเจ็บป่วยตั้งแต่ต้นเกมได้ง่ายๆ และการจะรักษาทำได้คือต้องปลดล็อกโรงหมอก่อนซึ่งค่อนข้างใช้เวลามาก ทำให้สุดท้ายชาวบ้านตายหมดก่อนที่คุณจะปลดโรงหมอได้ อะไรแบบนั้น) ซึ่งปัญหาในจุดนี้จริงๆ แล้วก็แก้ได้ง่ายๆ ที่ตัวคุณคือ คุณต้องวางแผนปลดล็อกสิ่งก่อสร้างที่จำเป็นกันตั้งแต่เริ่มต้นนั่นแหละ ควรจะต้องสร้างอะไรก่อน สร้างจำนวนเท่าไหร่ ใช้ประชากรเท่าไหร่ อันนี้คือเรื่องที่ต้องคิดและอาจจะต้องลองเล่นวนหลายรอบซักหน่อย ก็จะพอเข้าใจระบบของเกมเอง ความรู้สึกไม่สมดุลนี้อาจจะบอกว่ามันเป็นความท้าทายของตัวเกมและไม่ใช่ปัญหาในการออกแบบก็ได้เหมือนกันครับ  สำหรับข้อเสียหลักที่ทำให้คนเล่นบางส่วนให้โป้งแดงก็น่าจะเพราะว่า เวลาในตัวเกมค่อนข้างช้าแม้จะปรับความเร็วสูงสุดแล้ว ทำให้การกระทำอะไรหลายๆ อย่างในเกมต้องใช้เวลานานพอสมควร (เลยกลายเป็นเกมที่ต้องใช้เวลาเล่นมาก แต่ Progression เดินหน้าน้อย) แผนที่มีขนาดเล็กไปซักหน่อย ระบบค้าขายแสนธรรมดาที่ไม่หยืดหยุ่นนัก (เกมจะมีเผ่าอินเดียนแดงให้คุณติดต่อค้าขายหรือทำสัญญาเรื่องพื้นที่ด้วย แต่ต่างเผ่าก็ไม่ได้สร้างความแตกต่างอะไร) กราฟิกในเกมหากเปรียบเทียบกันมาตั้งแต่ช่วงที่เป็น Early Access จนกลายมาเป็นตัวเต็มก็ถือว่ามีการปรับปรุงให้ดูดีขึ้นกว่าเดิม แต่ถ้าหากนำไปเทียบกับเกมแนวเดียวกันทั่วไป กราฟิกในเกมนี้ดูจะยังขาดรายละเอียดไปในหลายๆ จุด พื้นผิวต่างๆ อย่างพื้นหญ้า แนวหิน หลายๆ อย่างขาดรายละเอียด ยิ่งถ้าเทียบกับเกมอย่าง Banished ด้วยแล้ว เกมนั้นดูจะมีรายละเอียดหลายๆ อย่างที่ดีกว่ามาก อีกทั้งตัวเกมยังไม่รองรับการแสดงผลแบบ Ultra Wide screen และมีเพียงตัวเลือกในการปรับ Resolution สูงสุดอยู่ที่ 1920x1080 25Hz เท่านั้น ซึ่งก็นับว่าแปลกที่ไม่มีตัวเลือกให้ปรับได้มากกว่านี้ แต่ถ้าหากคุณใช้จอภาพเพื่อเล่นที่ความละเอียด FHD การแสดงผลก็ไม่มีปัญหาอะไรครับ  แม้ [i]Depraved[/i]  จะไม่ได้สมบูรณ์แบบเท่ากับ [i]Banished[/i] ที่กลายเป็นเกมขึ้นหิ้งสำหรับคนเล่นเกมแนวสร้างเมืองไปแล้ว แต่ส่วนการสร้างและจัดการทรัพยากรทั่วไปก็ถือว่าสอบผ่านมาตรฐานสำหรับเกมแนวนี้อยู่ ดังนั้นถ้าคุณกำลังมองหาเกมที่เล่นได้สนุก ท้าทาย เป็นแนวสร้างเมืองที่มีรูปแบบการนำเสนอในธีมที่แปลกตาไม่ค่อยได้เห็นบ่อยนัก เกมนี้ก็ถือว่าโอเคอยู่ แม้คอนเทนด์และเกมเพลย์จะไม่ได้ล้ำลึกมากมายแต่สำหรับเกมที่พัฒนาด้วยทีมงานเพียงแค่ 2 คนซึ่งผมเฝ้ามองมาตั้งแต่เกมยังอยู่ใน Early Access มาจนถึงตอนนี้ ก็ถือว่าทำได้ดีเลยทีเดียวล่ะ Some have criticised FC:P for the 'lack of story' but as someone who enjoyed the Far Cry formula since FC2, I think I prefer it that way.   While I think Vass, Pagan, et al, are great characters, what keeps me coming back to the Far Cry series is the core game-play.  It's more than immersive - it transports me to another place (especially when I remove the HUD elements). It doesn't just allow for emergent game play - it encourages it. If anything, I find the 'story' elements often intrude on what is otherwise an almost zen like experience for me.   I understand that some may find it repetitive; I have certainly lost interest in Assassin's Creed, (and other Ubisoft products) which are in many ways very similar, but there is something about the Far Cry series that really has me hooked.  Steam controller works well, and there are a couple of good community configs, but I wish there was an official profile for the game.  Edit: The Final Boss Fights.  I won't change my recommendation because I absolutely loved Far Cry Primal, but the boss fight against Batari is a nightmare, and not in a good way.  I had played through the 'meat and vegetables' of the entire game: the side missions, defeating the villages, taming all the beasts etc (things that other might find grindy, but I love). I was taking my time, and really enjoying it till i was ready to end it and take down the two main bosses.  The first time I was defeated after a long battle. It was pretty grindy, so I left it for the night came back the next day, only to die again after getting Batari down to 1%. I must have hit her a dozen times with my mighty two handed club when she had hardly any health left, but she kept on coming, seemingly unharmed...  And I just didn't have the desire to go back again. I must be two missions off completing the entire thing, but I doubt now that I'll finish it.  It's such a shame. I love the Far Cry formula. I love taking each village, one by one; I love the emergent gameplay and the way the game allows you to play it your way. And UBI have shown they have the capacity to make really interesting side missions. So I can't understand why they insist on making these tedious boss fights.  It's not that they're all that difficult per se. They're just not fun.

KINGDOMS OF AMALUR HERE IT COMES THE RECKONING  Kingdoms of Amalur was a surprisingly good fantasy game. It has a fluid and fun combat system. It has a generic but decent storyline. But best of all, it has good side quests. Some of them are even more interesting then the main storyline at times.  What I liked most about Kingdoms of Amalur, personally... was how you could build your character in whatever way you wanted. You were not tied down to any restricted class. But you could cross-class between three different trees. Don't like what you ended up doing? No problem. You can re-spec your character at any time during the game. Gold is no object, as there seems to be an over abundance of it in the game. I finished the game with over 6 million pieces of dosh. If that gives you any idea how much money you can make in this.  The story goes like this. Your character gets killed doing something he or she shouldn't have been. You come back to life by some mysterious means... and you have the ability to control fate. Now it's time for you to go off and save the world. So yeah that's cool and all. We've heard this kind of plot before. But what is best about the game is the journey through it and the quests you undertake throughout. This game has good beefy side quests with rich story and characters. You wont be wasting your time like with a certain other game that just recently came out.. something with Dragons. Dragon Day I think it was called. Anyway, you'll find that there is a ton to do in this game. If you're a nut about completion this'll take you a good 100 + hours to complete. SO clear you calender, ya dig?  Weapons are cool. Each weapon has its own unique style and use. I suggest dicking around with all of them and seeing what you like best. I personally enjoyed the chakrams cause you don't see them much in games, and the daggers because they're the only weapons you can do killmoves with on a sneak attack.  The game has a big flaw however and this is one I don't usually complain about with games.. but it was too easy. At level 20... 40 being the max.. I was nigh invincible. It's too easy! I played on normal difficulty, so I recommend maybe playing on Hard if you're not new to RPG's and third person action games in general.  The DLCs were both great. Teeth of Narnia & Dead Kenan & Kel had a great storyline and plenty of extra and new content. I'd totally recommend picking up the complete package when it's on sale!  So am I missing something? Probably. If you have any questions regarding the game, let me know and i'll answer them post haste.  Finale Verdict: (4.4 out of 5)

I was looking for a game with controller support and this happened to be on sale and had very positive reviews. First off, the controller support is a joke. I could play the game just as well without any controller support with standard steam controller features. It is in large part a FPS and there is no aim assist when playing with a controller.  The unique selling point is the FPS mixing with a tower defense, but I must say that it is painfully obvious why TDs are usually from a top down RTS perspective. Flying enemies for example are very easy to overlook, because they are above you. The perspective also makes its hard to tell where hordes are going to spawn and which way they are going to take. The game only shows you where the first wave is going to go and successive waves might do something entirely differently.  Overall the game is terrible at explaining itself. It is so overexcited to get started that it is doesn’t explain its mechanics at all. How much damage does a tower/weapon do? What's its range? What type of enemy can it attack? How much HP do enemies have? Which enemies attack structures? Which enemies have what attack modifiers? What are combos/killing sprees and when do they happen? If the game contains this information, it hides it well. I had to discover everything through trial and error.   The gameplay is pleasant, but repetitive and gets old very fast. The FPS perspective has more downsides than upsides and does nothing to improve the genre. Has its charm, but is not a good TD game and after you take that away, what is left?

This is my first review ever - so please forgive me its flaws. I never considered writing a review however I am so delighted with this game it would be unfair to developers not to express in this modest way my appreciation for their creation. But enough with the intro. 	 Game is simple yet complex. It is somehow combination of Banished (survival in harsh and unfriendly environment, where you need to take close eye on resources and food), Civilization (hex based map with nice 3D elements and player-world interaction and turn-based mechanics) and card game (all encounters are resolved via card based tactical mechanic). Plus many elements of RPG.  What is most important to me and what makes this game unique is beautifully created world based on Slavic mythology with interesting and well refined story line, together with random side quests and events. It is obviously not a big production with high budget - yet game has something in it that makes you stay with it for one more turn, and then another, and another...  To sum up:  Pros:[list] [*] Big, interesting world based on Slavic mythology [*] Refined story line, side quests and random events [*] Pantheon of Slavic gods from who you can chose your patron - it has influence on your game [*] Card based encounters which encourages player to focus on tactic and development of his expedition forces [*] Many possibilities of item crafting  [*] RPG well combined with strategy and tactic [/list]  Cons: [list] [*] It consumes much more of your time that you would think... [*] At some point encounters with monsters are too easy when your squad is big enought and properly equipped [*] Sometimes world is created in frustrating way when you need to spend a lot of turns to get anywhere - basically you need to start a new game because of it [*] Magic aspect in the game especially when it comes to characters is unfortunately neglected (perhaps a good idea for a dlc) [*] Limited village development possibilities [*] I am really trying but can't find much more... [/list]  If you enjoy this type of strategy, tactic and hex map based games, and most of all you enjoy fantasy games - this game is a definitive must-have.   I hope developers will create some additional content, either a bigger DLC or expansion - game most certainly has a potential for further development. Fingers crossed!  Cheers.

Plus de 2h de jeu actuellement et il y a beaucoup à dire.  Ce que l'on remarque en premier c'est la pauvreté de choix dans les options, quelques options graphiques et c'est TOUT ! Aucune option pour le son ou possibilité de customisation des touches, ce qui nous oblige d'ailleurs à utiliser la technique célèbre du Alt+Shift pour passer le clavier en QWERTY et pouvoir jouer avec un minimum de confort. Je rajoute d'ailleurs le fait que les contrôleurs ne sont pas compatibles avec le jeu (mais je suis un adepte du clavier+souris donc ça ne me concerne point).   Passons aux graphismes: le jeu est très mal optimisé et les effets mal équilibrés ! Le framerate est inconstant, avec parfois de gros drops lors de situations stressantes qui pardonnent très mal ce genre de faiblesse. Le grain filmique est omniprésent et ne s'embarasse pas de la subtilité, surtout lorsqu'il est mixé avec d'autres effets de colorimétrie, d'aberration chromatique ou de flous tout aussi discrets ce qui peut vite rendre l'action illisible. Dommage car la DA n'est pas mauvaise et l'ambiance est plutôt immersive dans ses périodes de calme.   Ensuite le son: beaucoup de lacunes ici aussi. D'un côté nous avons des bruits ambiants manquant de subtilité, ce qui peut nous pousser rapidement à revoir le niveau sonore de notre casque à la baisse. Mais de l'autre côté nous avons également un manque cruel de son du côté du gameplay, rendant certaines actions du joueur confuses, lors du passage d'une arme à une autre par exemple.   Je ne parlerais pas pour le moment du scénario ou du gameplay pour le moment j'attendrais d'être plus avancé dans le jeu, voire de le finir, pour développer ces aspects (j'ai été freiné dans mon élan par un freeze sauvage dans un ascenceur, ne me laissant pas d'autre choix que l'implacable Ctrl+Alt+Suppr).  J'en concluerais donc en disant que je ne recommanderais pas Hollow dans son état actuel, mais si les dev snipent rapidement les problèmes cités ci-dessus alors....

I'll mostly talk about the changes to the Special Edition version of the game (short summary for base game: amazing character action game). There's a few new cutscenes, a bunch of new costumes (the original game didn't even have any additional costumes), and three new playable characters. The three new characters all share the feeling that they're much stronger than Nero and Dante, so easier difficulties start to feel rather redudant. But anyone familiar with the game would wanna choose the higher difficulties anyway.  - Vergil is the focus of the three new characters and he plays similar to how he does in DMC3. - Lady almost exclusively uses firearms so she feels like a very different but fun way of playing a character action game. - You switch to Trish halfway through Lady's campaign and she's the least interesting out of the three characters. She features a lot of attacks with a very wide range of attack which makes me think she was specificially made for Legendary Dark Knight mode.  Unfortunately, there's no new music (even when playing as the new characters, you still hear the same music as you would with Nero and Dante), and aside for a couple of minor additions to the end of the campaigns, you run through the exact same levels with the exact same enemy layouts when playing as the new characters. I wish they would have taken this opportunity to find some new way to mix up the gameplay with the enemies or levels. That said, the new characters play very differently from Nero and Dante, so they represent a lot of new gameplay even if the levels and enemy layouts are the same.  From a technical level, the Special Edition is surprisingly inferior to the original game. The original game feels like one of the most optimized games I've played on PC, but this new version runs at roughly half the framerate. However, since we're comparing to an absurdly well optimized game from 2008, this doesn't mean this new version has performance issues. Despite the weird drop in performance compared to the original game, any modern PC should have no trouble running the game at 60fps.  Another technical downgrade is the resolution support. The original game would run at virtually any resolution you threw at it, but not only is the resolution support limited in Special Edition, the game will outright crash at startup if Windows is set to support specific resolutions (for instance, it happens with 5120x2880).  And one omission compared to console versions of the original game (this was also missing in the PC port of the original game) are the leaderboards.  The new content easily outweighs the weird technical flaws. It just feels like the game is one patch away from feeling polished.

Although I've played DXHR back when it first came out, recently I got into Almost Human and felt the urge to replay the game...especially since the Director's Cut version had come out recently.  And now that I've finished it, I must say that I consider this is easily one of my most favorite games of all time.  Is it perfect?  Of course not.  But what this game *does* have is, interesting settings, compelling and very possible vision of a world in the near future, fascinating storyline and memorable characters....and all of that will stay with you long after the game's done.  There are multiple ways of going through each area to suit just about any playstyle out there; nooks and crannies to explore, secret areas to discover, emails to read, people to talk to, and sidequests to complete.  The game does not lock you into a specific playstyle, but rather makes it possible, through giving the player the ability to pick and choose their augmentations, to cater to and enhance, various ways of play.  Like to sneak around, hack into things and be virtually undetectable?  You can do that.  Like to just mow everyone down with explosions and heavy weapons?  You can do that too.  Don't like killing anyone?  Yes, you can be a pacifist and just knock people out.  One of the most interesting themes the game offers is the subject of the progress of technology and how it relates to us as humans.  Refreshingly, the game doesn't have a pre-determinted opinion on this and doesn't clobber you over the head with whatever it thinks is the right answer.  Rather, throughout the game, it allows you various glimpses and insights into different views from people you interact with, which affect your perception of the matter at hand, and, ultimately, play a huge role in how it all plays out in the end.  TL;DR - highly recommended, buy it and play it if you haven't already! :D

While everyone else is busy praising this game, I just fail to see the appeal.  In this game, you'll be jogging around trying to run errands for people that oftentimes are impossible if you don't know what you need ahead of the time. Running out of time to do stuff is common theme in this game, you'll be failing to meet quest deadlines, you'll lose your plants to season changes, you'll miss shops opening and closing. You have to keep a flippin' timetable so you know when to go crack these geodes. You'll have to go bend backwards to adhere to constraints you're given by the game.  I found myself being disinterested with social part of the game, so I decided to try out combat side of it. I was immensely disappointed to find out that the combat system is a heap of flaming garbage. Don't get me wrong, I appreciate good challenge and I've seen a lot of combat mechanics, from Prince of Persia (1989) sword dueling to DOOM (2016) glorykills. What we have here is unsatisfying, clunky, unwieldy combat system that feels like forklift attempting to fence. Enemies don't get slapped with nearly enough knockback when you block their attacks so you immediately get a follow-up hit as soon as your guard automatically drops. Lunging enemies will quite often get stuck in your hitbox, getting free hits on you while you try to move out of them at leisurely pace.  Moreover, game will downright punish you hard for losing, by not only taking your money, but your hard-earned items too, which I consider to be a BIG NO-NO for game heavily involving item-based progression. Grinding back your gear and money is not fun, nor relaxing and it generally is meant to waste my time, which is quite limited either way. Good thing you can flip the game off and shove TerminateProcess (with task manager or similar tool) down it's throat to roll the day back (No need for debugger or live memory editing, thankfully!).  Think about it for a second. I have to whip out OS tools to whack the game process in order to enjoy the game. Isn't this inherently wrong?  Let's sum it up. Game poses as a relaxing game but wants you to adhere to a strict schedule and allocate time very carefully. That sounds awful lot like work, the opposite of relaxation. Game poses as a fun game but it will not hesitate to punish you and take your hard-earned stuff away for you to grind to the same place again, not making any meaningful progress. That is cheap screw-you, opposite of fun. The game promises interesting local community, but instead I got bunch of needy flat characters ready to give me some menial tasks with success probability of the russian roulette. The game promised interesting cave to explore, I got hundred-something cookie-cutter levels full of annoying enemies and repetitive mining. Placing random rocks appears to be this game's pinnacle of procedural generation.  I simply fail to see the appeal. There are better time-waster games that treat player and player's time better, as paradoxically that may sound.

[b] Patch .5 Review [/b] TLDR; Excellent visuals, great combination of a Star Trek Sim and FTL: Faster Than Light, Solid Core gameplay IDEAS but balance/execution is lacking. For $20, I’d wait. Find it on sale or wait until the content increases.  [h1] Visuals: [/h1] At the very beginning I was slightly put off by the character portraits, they seemed like stickers plopped on to the uniforms and backgrounds. The second I got into the game and took a look around I quickly changed my tune. All of the stellar objects (planets, asteroids ect…) look stunning. Solar flares in-circling the stars, the surface of the planets well detailed and each one had its own character to it. The Command Chair view also has a ton of high points, if you ignore the character models and animations. The animations for the different command functions and even the simplified city all look superb. I can forgive the repeated characters (The command deck girls all look pretty much the same) I just hope they look to improve those in the future because against the rest of the game, it seems a tad out of place.   [h1]Story:[/h1] You’re the last hope of humanity running from the Scorn, your typical nomadic, devour everything in their path alien species. Pretty simple and not much explanation behind it.   [h1]Gameplay:[/h1] The core of the gameplay is fairly solid. Combat is fun and the exploration side has its strong points, but the UI and its responsiveness hurts me. Sometimes it seems that what I click on doesn’t register or does slowly. Assigning crew can be a bit of a learning curve for the first few times, and all the small numbers so close to one another can send your head into a spin. One feature I’d love is while assigned to a position, the relative skill number would appear alongside the name of the skill.  The Combat itself is fun and can be intense for the first play through or two until you start to get the hang of it, and even then it has its moments of excitement as you barely bring up shields in time or duck out of the way of a laser. Audio ques are well done, mostly on point and once you learn them, have a huge part in correctly defending yourself. The issue lies in variation, it turns into the same fight over and over again. A simple strategy emerges and the skill cap is frankly quite low. You may fight against 4-5 different ships but they all are fought the same way, by the end of the third play through I was taking almost no damage verses single combatants and maybe one shot when faced against two of them, even when I finally got a 3 ship encounter, I took maybe 3 hits. My request? Toss in some variation in strategy, in enemy modules or even change up the playing field, maybe an asteroid field could provide evading ships even better defenses? Not sure about how but I know a larger variation is needed or else it becomes stale quickly.   I love the resource management, even if it seems VERY overwhelming at first, a full tutorial would go a long way. Finding the correction combination of modules that suits your resource needs is a fun way to change up how you play and can decide if you really are going to stop at the planet or just book it to the next sector. The only complaint I have is the numbers on the civilization side aren’t always very clear, the biggest one being the growth stat. I have a growth of .9%! Okay, is that .9% of my population every day? Week? Month?? None seem to be quite right. Or is it not supposed to be a %, and it’s just + .9 population every day? This last one seems to be the case, but it took until my third play through to come to that conclusion.  To round things off, I love how the game makes you work for your victories, or at least seem like it. I played three runs on normal (each run seems to last 3-4 hours with the slower, more resource efficient engine) and I felt like I earned the two victories I got. I just want a climax, both times I pretty much coasted into the finish line with nothing stopping me (Abit, the second time I was bleeding population with 0 food left :D).  [h1]Closing[/h1] Overall, a great game for someone like me who is absolutely obsessed with space exploration and sim games, the average person might want to wait a bit longer, or pick it up for a few play throughs and come back later when the game receives more content. If you enjoyed FTL: Faster Than Light and have always dreamed of being the next Kirk or Picard, this is a must pick up.  [b]Verdict: 7/10[/b] with tons of potential. I’ll do my best to keep up with the updates and revise as changes come along

If you purchase Daymare expecting something like Resident Evil 2, you will disappointed...because Daymare is an indie project and of course developers couldn't counf on the amout of money needed for a triple A project. But if you consider it for what it is, an indie survival horror done with the sole purpose to pay homege to classic masterpieces like Resident Evil 2, Daymare can provide a lot of fun. The game is decently long, around 10 hours for three playable characters. The best thing of the titles are the puzzles, which are never stupid, never too hard and very well balanced. The graphics are ok, I guess, with the character's models being not so great, mostly to the lack of details and animations, but really you couldn't expect more here considering what I wrote above. The location instead are very good, atmospheric and well designed. There are some problems in and here, like textures which won't load from time to time making very hard to read something on the hud, but the price is just about right for the amount of content provided. There's also an additional mode which is basically The 4th Survivor from Resident Evil 2, with two maps (for now) and other maps coming. If you are hungry for a good survival horror, Daymare can provide you some hours of  fun. It's not perfect, but it's very enjoyable.

I almost forgot to post a review of this game to illustrate why it is in fact quite an uninspiring reboot which only manages to give some impression of the original. My motivations;  - The graphics, although quite current-gen, are like plastic. They fail to give a feeling of the gore and roughness of hell and instead you feel like you're walking around in a gum-ball-world-gone-evil which tries but fails. - The action is mostly initiated by scripted instances in which monsters spawn which you have to kill and then some door opens. 3 minutes into the game the first such instance starts. I remember hoping this was just to give you a feeling for the gameplay. But this is what Doom 2016 is mostly about. You go in some room, kill the monsters, and walk through the next door. If you don't know where to go, you press the help-button. - The story is okay. You can definately see a lot of work went in the end-bosses too. But all of this failed to compensate for the full package. Which lacks a real challenge and simply feels like halfway the developers were told to skip the real game and meet the deadline.   Recommended to buy when 60% off retail price.

GRID 2 is highly recommended for fans of the racing genre. I have thoroughly enjoyed it and I think anyone who likes the Codemasters or NFS series this should be a no brainer.  PROS - - Huge variety in cars, tracks and race types - Graphics - Damage modelling - Paint job customization - Driving model - Rewind feature  CONS - - No race line feature - Car spins during painting - Driving model  If you noticed that I put the driving model as both a pro and a con, it's because really the model is subjective. It is not a 'hardcore' model like you will find in other high end racers. Nor is it too arcady. Like I said, if you enjoy NFS etc, this fits in well with those.  The rewind feature is a huge step forward to reduce frustration in racing games. Ever run the perfect race only to make a small error at the last lap and get dumped to the end of the pack? That's over. Have a crash or take a corner wrong and spin out? Just rewind a few seconds and have another go at it. Feel that's cheating? Don't use it. Personally, I love the option.  Cars look great, tracks look great. Track your best times and stats against your Steam friends. I haven't used the multiplayer much, but its there if that's your thing.   Get bored of racing? Try the demolition derby! You'll have lots of fun with this one.

Problem is, most of these reviews seem to be about those things, rather than Anno 2070 itself.  This game is incredibly good, in my opinion.  Seriously, it's SimCity meets Command & Conquer; what fan of strategy games wouldn't like that?  Start with one small town with some fisheries on an island, and expand and grow into a massive, sweeping empire spanning the map.  Complex and richly detailed production lines for goods to satisfy your citizens' needs, interesting NPCs with unique (if a tiny bit stereotypical) personalities, and intense struggles against other empires on military, economic, and diplomatic fronts, all while trying to keep your islands from becoming so polluted they spawn huge natural disasters... or technological ones like oil spills and nuclear power plant explosions!  To anyone reading this who hasn't tried this game yet: as a lifelong fan of strategy games in all forms, I will tell you right now, it is absolutely worth putting up with the stupid DRM and UPlay nonsense to play Anno 2070.  While the haters hate, I'll be happily buried up to my eyebrows in this awesome game.

I developed a little pre-bed-time ritual the week after buying Polynomial 2.  Putting on my VR headset, I'd fire up the game and continue the survival mode.  After clearing out all but one of the slower enemies in the first wave I'd pick a direction with an interesting swirl of glittering spiral clouds pulsing in time to the music and accelerate towards it.  The stardust flew by and blue comets blazed to life then fractured into fading pieces before disappearing from sight.  The universe of The Polynomial 2 stretches around me and it's a peaceful, relaxing, and very pretty way to wrap up the day.  Then I'd reload and blast through as many waves as possible amidst a storm of lasers and the geometrically-exploding particle remains of enemy ship-creatures, because who can resist one last torrent of neon lightshow streaming directly through the eyeballs before calling it a day?
It's not a single player game for sure, but with a few friends and a server it is great fun! I've enjoyed my time, but do note, this is not a masterpiece by any standard.

As a whole, doing everything that you can in this game, the mediocrity outweighs the good. Pick and choose those good parts as much as you can to change that ratio.  The main story is great and the the two cities you'll be exploring are filled with details to absorb. But although on the surface there seems to be a wealth of minigames and substories to do, they quickly feel like boxes to mark on a checklist (because they are, for CP), rather than something to do out of actual enjoyment. Also the combat leaves much to be desired, you are practically obligated to look up online guides to figure out where/how to get some substories/business upgrades/best items, and all those small unskippable cutscenes can really add up.  Again, the game's main story is excellent and the voice acting is well delivered, the cut scenes are very stylized and the action is great. However I felt that the story only really started to pick up between halfway and two thirds of the way through the story (there are 16 chapters). But to the game's credit I could be a bit biased on that, since I started maxing out all of Kiryu's and Majima's businesses at that point.  The variety of minigames are alright, and the over-the-top animations for some mundane actions like answering a telephone or jumping into the driver's seat of an arcade machine can be pretty funny. The karaoke even has some music videos starring the main characters singing the songs in the background, though it's a bit tough to focus on when playing the game. Hell, the claw machine even accurately represents how frustrating those damn things are in real life! Unfortunately these minigames tire themselves out rather quickly; and there isn't much incentive, fun wise or reward wise, to do them more than a few times.   The combat isn't very fun. Generic enemies aren't much of an issue (unless they have weapons guns or especially bladed weapons), but big boys or bosses can constantly tank your regular hits. Heavy attack guard breaks don't really work on them, or if they do you're stuck in a follow-through animation for too long, and they put their guard back up before you can get some hits in. So the game expects you to go on the defensive and dodge their attacks and try to get behind them for an attack... but their hyper armor and crazy tracking followup attacks just feel like they hit you anyway. If you do spend 10 seconds waiting for them to attack, then dodging their attacks, you can only get like 3 hits in before they go back into turtle mode.   So, for boss enemies, don't even bother fighting them with your fists. Just look for a guide on how to get slime/zap/smoke guns from Majima's Dragon & Tiger minigame and sidestep the terrible boss combat altogether. You can't use items or weapons in the Coliseum, avoid that as much as possible lmao.  But yeah you'll be doing a lot by the way - Googling for guides that is. The Dragon & Tiger thing is arcane as hell. And with how long this game is and how much side-content it has, you can't just play it without a guide and feel like you got a good glimpse of all the content and not feel like you wasted hours of your time running all over the place ineffectually. Also some substories are outright unbeatable without looking up a guide, like bowling a turkey for an advisor, or the entirety of the pocket circuit substory (which also requires some BS RNG item from the dream machines).  Lastly is what feels like a nitpick to me, but it just adds up too much to ignore: Character dialogue pauses, unskippable cutscenes, and load screens are all over the place. Sure some of the over-the-top animations - like mounting up on an arcade machine - are hilarious the first few times you see them! But all those unskippable dialogues and animations seriously wear you down when all you want to do is retry bowling a turkey, or take a taxi somewhere, or win a danceoff, or dodge some asshole's attacks in a fight, or ...everything.  All in all, again, I feel that this game is really only worthwhile for the main story; you should stick to the main story as much as possible and ignore as many substories and minigames as you possibly can. Not that some of the substories don't have their moments, but it all just feels like they're such an investment just for a weak sitcom laugh, with no voice acting to even sell the joke. Maybe you can enjoy them as some simple mindless thing to do while listening to a podcast or something, after you beat the main game, idunno man.

What a game!  It's exactly what any fan of the franchise could want it to be. The story is well fleshed out, thematically wonderful and right on point for a Terminator story. It includes all those parts you'd want in such a tale, the menace of the machines is conveyed terrifically, the enemies very well designed, especially the humanoid terminators with their relentless, awful advances and merciless attacks. Wonderful.  The characters are well designed and well acted. You root for your friends, and you want to see them right. You have real choices which affect what happens to them, and I think that's great.  Gameplay is fun, the guns could have been lifted from the original Terminator movie, as could the sets. I couldn't say that the post-apocalyptic setting is beautiful, because it's not meant to be, but it is spectacularly well designed, with real attention to detail. There are some role-playing elements, but they are somewhat limited and not game-wrecking, but that's not a problem. There is crafting, which I didn't use much, weapon modification, which I did, but this was, again, somewhat limited.  If I have one gripe with the game, and it's a very, very small one, it's that the roleplay and customisation options feel half-complete. They could have done with a bit more to make them stand out, and the sight options for the weapons weren't terrific, and you could not alter them. They came with the gun, and you were stuck with them. I also dislike the level cap, but these are very small points.  As a FPS, it is terrific, with a great story, fantastic visuals and enough surprises to keep you playing to the end. As a Terminator property, it is nearly transcendent, especially when you take into account the rubbish we've had lately. The best thing in the franchise since T2, and a must for any fan. It's not vastly long, I completed it in about 9 hours, and that's with all the side quests and everywhere explored. Even so, I don't consider my money wasted, not by a long way. I bought it on sale, but I would have happily paid full price, it was that good.  This felt like a real labour of love by the studio, and I hope they make a sequel. I would really love to see the story continue.  9/10.

Fantastic concept, fantastic execution.  I've been a big fan of board games ever since my high-school buddies and I started to get together on Friday nights to play Eclipse. When college came around, however, we could no longer get together and play since I moved out of state. I didn't realize how much I missed board games until I picked up TTS during its last sale. I was originally skeptical about the game's ability to provide intuitive controls for manipulating various game pieces, but boy was I wrong. While TTS is primarily a physics sandbox and doesn't necessarily enforce game rules (it's up to the players to play a fair game), it does incorperate a whole lot of tools, resources, and code to allow games to be played just as they would in real life if not better. The ability to stack and shuffle card decks, hide your hand, flip individual pieces, etc. means that tasks that might ordinarily require a lot of fiddling and potentially make a mess become nothing more than a few simple hotkey-presses. I've yet to play any long-winded games like Eclipse (Maybe once finals are over XD), My experience with TTS thus far has shown that it is very easy to use and incredibly fun. I'd definitely recommend it to my old friends so we can play games together again.  Pros: - Board games - Online multiplayer, for when you have no friends ;_; - Steam Workshop support - Can join any game and mods will auto-download and cache - Cosmic Encounter DLC (I have the physical game. It's fantastic) - Easily create quality custom content  Cons: - Voice chat could use expansion (e.g. Indicator above player profile pic when chatting rather than in sidebar) - Playing in a virtual environment (esp. with strangers) can feel less socially satisfying - Morally questionable in regards to playing published games for free off the Workshop  Finally, it's important to note that the game is still being updated and improved, and the devs still have a lot to put into the game before they're finished. The list of future improvements and Kickstarter goals can be found on their site if you're still skeptical about the future of the game's development.

The Great Wobo Escape: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~     We must be desperate for resources lately.  We have created an automated mining factory in space for goodness sake, where cute, little white robots are mining. How do we know they are mining the right stuff for us? No-one knows really. All we‘ve been told is that there are big, red robots with zapping devices that supervise the colony. What do we call them? Oh yes, the watchers. Well, everything was peachy until one of these robots, named Wobo, decided to make a run for freedom.  The Great Wobo Escape is a side-scrolling adventure game combined with a touch of stealth where you control a white robot named Wobo.  The game offers eight stages and three levels: Normal (where you can save your progress by using scanners along the way), Hardcore (you can’t save your progress at all; if you die, you’ll spawn back to the start of the stage), and Time trial (in this mode of difficulty, you must finish the stage by a specific time).  The first stage is really a tutorial and will show you how to control Wobo either by using your keyboard or gamepad. One of the aspects I really like about this game is that anyone of any age can play it due to the fact that there is no violence at all. It is simple and fun to play. Nonetheless, you need to be careful not to be caught by these big, red robots with electric shock guns. If you are caught, Wobo will be zapped into pieces. As you progress through the game, you will notice faint images of Wobo in between structures here and there. There are locations where your robot can hide and avoid these nasty red robots. You also have obstacles to worry about, such as pressure smoke coming out of pipes, damaged electric cables, moving platforms and more. There are levers and terminals to activate which can open doors to new areas as well as cutting off the electricity and pressure in pipes, which will resolve the issue with the pressure smoke. You also have to free other woblings (small robots) within each of the stages and you’ll be rewarded with extra points at the end of each level.  You also have puzzles or mini games to complete; they are pretty obvious and give this game a bit more to its overall content.  Graphically, the game looks very good and runs well. In terms of the controls they are responsive, whether you’re using the keyboard or the gamepad. It terms of the length of the game, you’ll be finishing your first walkthrough in about two and a half hours on the normal difficulty. There is a bit of re-playability with the hardcore and time trial modes.    Positives: ~~~~~~~   -	Nice graphics  -	Fun and easy to play for all ages -	Nice and friendly mini games (puzzles) -	Good price point -	Achievements  Negatives: ~~~~~~~~   -	No trading cards -	A bit short  Definitely a great game to introduce to your children, and fun to play as an adult!  7/10  Key provided by developer/publisher for review purposes. Dark Old Sun: ~~~~~~~~~~    The Earth is in crisis! All energy resources are about to hit rock bottom and the fate of humanity is hanging by a thread! Meanwhile, a group of astronomers has identified a rather strange black star that emanates extremely bright light. This small star appears to have an abundance of energy which surely would save humanity from extinction if it could be harvested! They figured out how to extract this energy safely and bring it back to the citizens of Earth. This second chance at life has indeed been celebrated by everyone, including warlords, one of whom has managed to steal one of the biggest and most powerful spaceships of the human fleet, The VoidWalker! What is he up to now? Oh, Dark Old Sun!  Dark Old Sun is a Shoot’Em up game where you take control of one of six vessels and your goal is to destroy the VoidWalker in order to win the game.  The game has of several modes of play.  The Story and Arcade modes are basically the same, with the small difference that you’ll be told a story (in writing) between stages. There are 6 stages in these modes and you’ll be able to choose your level of difficulty (normal, hard or extreme) as well as choosing how to upgrade your vessel within the stages (classic or advanced). If you choose the classic option, your spaceship will receive automatic upgrades, while the advanced option will give you the choice of what to upgrade or change on your vessels at any given time, as long as you have collected enough golden crystals to do so.   In the survival mode, you have to eliminate wave after wave of enemies for as long as you can until your death! The difficulty level will increase after each wave - a tough mode, to be really honest with you, which is great! The third one is the challenge mode which has short games based on retro titles - they are great fun and hard. I’ll let you discover them!  The gameplay in the Story and Arcade mode is pretty good. As I mentioned above, you have to go through 6 challenging stages. What I really like about this game is the fact that you can move your ship all around the screen as well as rotating it to shoot at enemy vessels wherever they happen to appear. Each time you destroy an enemy ship, a few golden crystals will appear at that location and will start falling down towards the bottom of your screen. Move your ship onto these crystals to collect them; pick up as many as possible, as you’ll need plenty of crystals to upgrade your ship.  Your spaceship will be equipped with primary and secondary weapons. There are 5 to choose from for each category (primary and secondary) and you can change them at any given time without using your golden crystals.  Drones are basically your super weapons and when activated, will help you go through difficult sections of the game, but only for a certain period of time.  There are a total of four drones to choose from and you can swap from one to another without using any golden crystals. You also have 3 types of ability and can upgrade your armour and generator.  You’ll start using your crystals when you want to upgrade specific attributes. For example, you might decide to upgrade from one to five projectiles from your primary or secondary weapons.  You can also upgrade the drone’s lifetime, as well as your armour and generator. All of these options will cost a certain number of golden crystals, so keep shooting at the enemies!  Within each of the stages, the game will automatically save three times. The first two will give you additional golden crystals and regenerate your life (shield/armour, in this case). The third save will occur just before the boss fights. Boy they are fun, but they can be frustrating, especially while playing the hard or extreme difficulty levels. In any case, each of the bosses has to be defeated three times in order to win the fight.  And yes, their looks and style of fighting will vary within each of these three phases of combats.  Graphically, the games looks good and runs very well. The soundtrack is great too, which is always a plus!  The content is very good for the asking price and this game offers great re-playability! [b][h1]DEVO, NÃO NEGO, PAGO SE PUDER![/h1][/b]  [b][u]História:[/u][/b] Tudo de passa numa noite na cidade de Salem, Massachusetts. Você é Ronan O’Connor, um ex-delinquente  ex-policial agora-fantasma. Em busca de um serial killer, você vai parar num sótão aonde pessoas informaram que o Bell Killer estava. Chegando lá, você é assassinado pelo mesmo, dando início ao jogo.    Nesse momento você descobre que o ditado “suas dívidas serão quitadas em sua morte” é falso, e que você precisa descobrir quem lhe matou e o porquê, só assim sendo possível ir para o Paraíso. Enquanto isso, você está preso na Terra vagando igual a uma Alma Penada.    Com o passar da história, você desvendará os motivos das mortes, o motivo do Bell Killer existir, e o que lhe aguarda no final fará a sua cabeça dar umas mini-explosões de tão inesperado que o final é.  [b][u]Gameplay:[/u][/b] Não se engane, Murdered: Soul Suspect é um Collect-A-Thon. O jogo possui o caso principal que é desvendar a sua morte, mas possui uma dezena de casos secundários que explicarão o passado da cidade e suas outras tragédias mortais.  -  Todos os casos secundários se resumem em explorar a cidade/local da missão(apartamento, delegacia e afins), revelar a evidência que está no mesmo plano que você (mas que não está no plano dos vivos, os quais não conseguem enxergar o mundo do mesmo modo que você) e coletá-las. Ao coletar todas, você resolve o caso secundário. Existem cerca de 5 casos de pessoas que estão no limbo e que, antes de subirem ao Paraíso, devem descobrir a causa da morte. Você as ajuda, caso queira, e também não passa de uma missão de coletar evidências. -  Já o caso principal se resume em procurar pistas num cenário restrito, unir as evidências e assim revelar o que aconteceu ali, progredindo cada vez mais no jogo.   -  Você pode possuir pessoas para escutar o que elas estão fazendo, ver pelos olhos delas para achar alguma evidência, e até mesmo influenciar a pessoa a ter algum pensamento que irá ajudar a progredir o caso.  -  Existem inimigos no jogo, mas são bem poucos e aparecem em poucos momentos (não passaram de 5, pelo que me lembro). São Demons que, para derrota-los, você deve chegar sorrateiramente por trás deles e exorcizá-los.   [b][u]Trilha Sonora:[/u][/b] Praticamente inexistente. Mas os sons ambiente são muito bem feitos e lhe passam a sensação de estar em uma cidade mal-assombrada.    [b][u]Conclusão:[/u][/b] Murdered: Soul Suspect é um ótimo jogo e algo novo em seu gênero, mas que foi injustamente massacrado pela crítica. É, com certeza, [b]um dos “Must Play” de 2014[/b]. Pode não valer R$99, mas é indispensável caso encontre-o por menos de R$30.   [b][u]Notas:[/u][/b] Não jogue-o esperando achar que a investigação é igual L.A. Noire. Aqui não tem nada de interrogar, nem detectar se o suspeito está mentindo e muito menos falhar em um caso porque você errou nas evidências. Murdered é um jogo [u]linear[/u] que quer contar uma história. Caso você seja uma pessoa que preze Gameplay sobre História, esse jogo não é para você!

Наш подопечный – Джакс, бывший легендарный командир альбов (неигровая враждебная фракция), но при этом полный обсoс, который с трудом справляется с монстрами первого ранга (их четыре). Формально, у героя частичная амнезия и потеря навыков из-за прекращения приёма элекса, но это такое себе оправдание, тем более, можно найти отчёты, где сказано, что все прекратившие принимать элекс умерли, однако это никак не развивается, т.е. вроде Джакс и особенный, но всё равно обсoс. Он так же необычайно туп, в одном задании местный авторитет просит оплатить проигрыш, для чего передаёт деньги и некий презент. Наверняка вы уже догадались, что это за презент, но Джакс – нет. В диалоге нельзя высказать жертве свои подозрения, а после выполнения квеста слышен взрыв, гг же всё равно задаёт вопрос “а что было в коробке”, тут я словил квадро фейспалм. Наш подопечный в одном диалоге расспрашивает о самых базовых вещах, а в другом сам рассказывает какие-то детали о происходящем. Ещё есть холодность, вне зависимости от уровня которой, герой бубнит монотонно заунывным голосом. Да у Адама Дженсона больше эмоций. Эта самая холодность нужна лишь для того, чтобы высосать из игры три финала. При том, что в конце случается Масс Эффект и намёк на продолжение (в котором я что-то сомневаюсь). Некоторые пассивки завязаны на эту характеристику. Парадокс, что её уровень указан в цифрах, а сама характеристика – нет, вот “сентиментальный” это много или мало, а в цифрах, 32, 59, 71? С навыками беда, много откровенно бесполезных. Даже король рпг – взлом замков - ибо в сундуках мусор. По той же причине неинтересно исследовать карту, сплошная копипаста: бутылочка и немного хлама, присыпанных щепоткой элексита, в зданиях ещё обязательная записка с белибердой в содержимом; а шанс найти уникальное оружие под свой класс таков, что проще фотомодель закадрить будучи прыщавым девственником. По-прежнему нужно искать учителей, но они не дадут полезного совета, не обладают уникальным набором доступных к изучению навыков, даже при плохом отношении не откажутся обучать. Сюжет не впечатляет, серьёзно, твист в котором бы главгадом оказался робот-пылесос, столько раз мелькавший в заставках, более впечатлил. Квестовые задания обставлены неплохо (тут и традиционные поиски юниторов-преобразователей присутствуют), но на начальном этапе решение упирается в три варианта: драка (шансов ноль), деньги (эй, я вообще-то заработать пришёл), навык, который ещё не получен. Так же не дают никакого представления о том, насколько сложным может оказаться задание. А почему? Переходим к главному гробу игры – боевой системе. На циферки урона можете даже не смотреть, они бесполезны, вся соль кроется в улучшении оружия, без чего противникам более высокого ранга, чем ваша пушка, вы просто не будете наносить урон. Проблема усугубляется тем, что враги натыканы рандомно, пиная какого-нибудь свинокрыса или падальщика вполне можно привлечь тролля (существа тут иначе называются, но это простой ренейм). А т.к. гг может бегать и имеет джетпак (единственное решение, которому я рад ибо дебильные стрефы срабатывают когда угодно, кроме как в бою – разрабы не освоили ещё кнопочку “перекат” – так что без неё ачивка “мастер по лепёшкам” была бы получена первой), то монстры кидаются магическими какахами. Удивительно, но при полном отсутствии намёка на баланс разрабы сотворили несколько уровней сложности. Зачем, и так можно бесконечно варить элексовый напиток, дающий очки характеристик! With all the depressing and dull-colored games out there, it's great to find a positive and brightly-colored one.  This game is not only that, but has created a fascinating world to explore filled to the brim with weird and whimsical creatures.  The player is drawn into this fantastic world, and then forced to watch as it is brutally disemboweled.  Of course, it all works out in the end, but still it's quite the gut-punch.  Most importantly though, it not only tackles a moral not often touched on in games, but it tackles it really well.  There's an interactive flashback sequence that lays it on the line, but doesn't hamfist it down your throat.  I'm probably not doing it any favors describing it so vaguely, but I don't really want to spoil it for anyone.  Just know that you'll be thinking about it for quite a few hours after you play it.  While the game shares the same tone as the classic 90's 3d platformers, it definitely doesnt play like one.  It's pretty much the indie game scene's answer to Assassin's Creed.  Whether this is awesome or awful is totally up to the player.  I personally didnt mind it, but people looking for a straight-up platformer might be disappointed.  But if you're looking for a gorgeous world with neat characters and a sweet story, then you should give The Last Tinker a try.

Siendo un viejo jugador de aventuras gráficas y habiendo pasado casi por todas: Monkey Island, Simon The Srocerer, Sam&Max, Larry, Kyrandia, King Quest, Indiana Jones FoA, etc. me siento calificado para dar mi opinion.  Sinceramente comencé Deponia con muchas ganas por las buenas criticas que tenía y esos hermosos graficos realizados a pulso.  Pues bien, separemos algunos aspectos:  1_Los graficos son preciosos, el arte, los colores, los diseños, estan muy muy bien diseñados con una mezcla de dibujo manual y animaciones flash pero que encajan bastante bien.  2_La musica es bastante alegre y acompaña a la aventura de manera correcta, sobresaliendo algún que otro track.  3_El humor, pues para algunos es excelentes, pero para mi es bueno con, tintes infantiloides, chistes reciclados y previsibles y que en momentos roza lo mediocre, pero ojo, no es malo, pero tampoco excelente a mi gusto.  4_La historia esta bastante bien, es un tanto original, fresca y recuerda mucho a los tipicos cuentos de aventuras de antaño. De todas formas tampoco es la gran panacea, donde se podria resumir, que controlamos a un huerfano sin hogar, un vago altruista que aspira escapar de ese basurero en el que habita, tal como cree que lo hizo su padre.  Sacando esos aspectos, queda la estructura y programación del juego, y pienso que es bastante desastrosa...veamos:  1_Animaciones tiene muyyy poquitas, practicamente solo veremos las de nuestro personajes, que encima por momentos es brusca y torpe.  2_El audio y los movimientos de boca no estan bien desarrollados, amen de esto, en muchos momentos veremos como los personajes hablan pero ni se le mueven los labios y estan esáticos.  3_Las acciones dentro del juego estan un tanto mal desarrolladas, muchas veces pasa que queremos combinar un objeto con otro y ni siquiera le han programado un dialogo, por lo cual no menciona nada; otras veces realiza acciones repetidas sin tener coherencia con lo que estamos queriendo hacer y esto pasa mucho.  4_Los puzzles son de lo peorcillo que he visto, estos mismos no tienen coherencia y son alocados (vease atrapar un cepillo de dientes viviente con una trampera de ratones), pero bueno, esto podría ser perdonado ya que muchas aventuras de calidad como Monkey Island lo tenian, pero una cosa es que sean puzzles alocados y otra es cuando esto se combina con puzzles incongruentes y para nada lógicos, donde si bien muchas veces recibimos pistas de como proceder, otras veces nos quedaremos atascados hasta que por prueba y error los solucionemos. Pero como dije, no he tenido una buena experiencia con ellos, ni tampoco satisfaccion al completarlos por ser un menjunje de sinsentidos.  4b_Dentro de los puzzles nos encontraremos con varios miniujuegos, que tambien pecan por no tener logica alguna, donde solo se resumen a prueba y error, vease al apuntar el arpon en la primera parte, o luego cuando tenemos que detonar unas bombas en determinadas zonas del pueblo para que suenen las alarmas de las casas. Considero que son puzzles metidos a saco, para alargar la aventura y no aportan nada interesante, sino mas bien, todo lo contrario, terminan siendo frustrantes y tediosos.  Todavia no lo he terminado, puede que cuando lo haga cambie mi perspectiva, pero no lo creo. Esperaba mucho más de Deponia, y lo que me he encontrado es un lobo vestido de oveja, es decir, un título que en su superficie parece una obra maestra, con una musica y sonidos muy buenos, unos graficos hermosos con dibujos hechos a mano, pero cuando se empieza a rascar un poco se descubre una aventura bastante mediocre, sin sentido, con puzzles torpes, sin lógica y sin coherencia; muchos defectos de programación y ejcución.  Una aventura que, lo que dure la pasarás algo bien e incluso te diviertas un poco descubriendo su mundo y personajes, pero que pasará sin pena y sin gloria.  Edito: Vale, lo he terminado y luego de la primera zona, la del pueblo el jego y los puzzles se hacen más llevaderos y no tan tediosos como la primera parte. Ahora puedo decir que está bastante bien, le doy un 7.5 pero no más por los problemas que expuse mas arriba.

I have to throw in a review just to offset all the uninformed negative reviews I see popping up recently. You build your character decks up slowly over time, so people who want instant gratification will not enjoy this aspect.  Each character deck IS the character, so the intent is not to change the entire deck every new adventure, but to tweak it to your liking with the new cards that you will gain from adventuring (if you spend the turns to do so...sometimes you just have to skip gaining items in order to close a location in time to win). It is unfair to compare this game to most other card/deckbuiling games. It is more like DnD roleplaying game using cards to represent weapons/armor/items/spells/allies and the blessings are sort of like wildcards/boosters. The cards also represent the health of your character. Warriors have fewer in their hand and so are less likely to die from wounds but have fewer choices. Mages are the opposite...many cards in hand (potentially dangerous) but more options in a turn.  I could go on and on, but I really just wanted to leave a positive review to offset some of the negative ones - especially if you have only played a few minutes...how in the world can you leave an informed review.  A tip for new players - even though you can have 1 to 6 characters in your party, stick with 3 (maybe 4) if you want an little easier game. 1 or 2 will usually leave you lacking in needed abilities and 5 or 6 really presses you on time to complete the scenario. After a few games you will see what I mean. Give it a chance and you will be plesantly surprised.

In short, I enjoyed playing this game, it was more enjoyable than I originally thought it would be. Before I go on though I would point out that, I am very much the targeted demographic being a huge fan of this style of gameplay, having finished the souls series multiple times. Also note that I played the entire game using an Xbox 360 controller so I cannot confirm how well the keyboard handles.  Pros: •	Level design is well done, and encourages short cuts •	The combat is immediately familiar and holds up to other titles in the genre •	The weapon and item selection is quite varied allowing for replayability •	Every single boss is good, some even great (Alpha Twin = Prince Lothric?) •	The artefact choice at the beginning is great (needs to be a way to swap them) •	From first glance, the builds that are possible seem varied and extensive •	Dash into enemy to stun is a great mechanic whilst not perfect •	The story whilst not perfect is surprisingly interesting, and a great take on the whole hero keeps resurrecting idea that the souls games are known for •	Not to spoil anything but the challenges to get more healing is something I personally really like.  Cons: •	Dash is not the most accurate of movements which causes some issues in both traversing the level and during combat •	Resting resets the state of your weapon •	Door mechanics can occasionally force an area reset •	Some enemy attacks can be hyper specific at any distance (Prisoner One Laser Beam) •	There is the occasional attack which does not give any time to react leading to some unfair deaths (Toxic grenade, Psycher Rifle) •	Parrying seems a bit too easy (maybe just me?) •	There needs to be some obvious rest point after a boss which isn’t always the case •	Blocking does not seem to stagger enemy chain attacks •	The mimic enemies are too random and I was mostly annoyed by them  Bugs: •	Small thing where going up an elevator into the hub section, before the elevator even arrives you can move the camera like you are walking normally before you are even in the level. •	There were two points where I had to reset the level as a door closed as an enemy on the other side of it had seen me •	The biggest issue by far is that the final boss in the ship got stuck on walls a whole bunch, which ended the fight prematurely for me  Summary I beat the game in 8 hours, and I did not feel I was rushing, the time whilst not huge is fine for a game like this as the levels don’t vary significantly and the game does not want to waste your time. Because of the 2D plane the combat whilst enjoyable is not as nuanced as something like dark souls, and the shorter time means that it does not get exhausting like a 20-hour game would. In summary, I don’t think the game is for everyone but souls/ soulsborne fans will enjoy it, I personally would pay full price for this but getting it during a sale would be even better especially if people see value for time put into a game as it is not the longest of experiences. I would love to see more of this, especially some kind of local/ online vs mode.

(Spoiler free review.)  Just buy it. I don't care if it isn't on sale. If you have $10 for a game, just buy Undertale. You can skip the soundtrack, just pickup this game up. No, avoid Let's Plays as you will only ruin the experience. Just go with it.  The game itself is a solid 6-7+ hours of gameplay with wonderful, mostly comical characters that are always enjoyable to be around. The plot is simple compared to other jRPGs, but I will personally take such a plot if it means that each line of dialog is well written. Also a pleasant stray from what is typical of the genre is that the game is fast paced with no noticeable moments where they game drags. If you are walking down a long hall, there is probably a reason. Add in the fact that I don't think I grinned at all and you have a game without any kind of padding. And with the overarching theme it has, Undertale doesn't act preachy. Sure, there is a line suggesting something about this theme, but the game doesn't say anything revolutionary. (Or at least, it showed nothing to for me.)  Combat is also interesting for the genre. While, again, not revolutionary, the mercy system as entirely plausible manner of playing this game. When choosing to avoid combat, you can interact with the monsters to try and negotiate your way out. These interactions range from trying to talk to them, complimenting, criticizing, and even flirting as well as others. All of which depends on the monster you are targeting with results that will vary on a few things. Going the mercy route results in you not killing the monster, but nets you no EXP. Always an option though is to fight, which is a basic: a bar going across the screen and you needing to stop it right when it lands in the middle for maximum damage. Beyond that though, equipment selection is limited and there are no alternative attacks. Then when monsters attack, you get full movement to dodge. While it can be difficult at times, it is entirely possibly to dodge entire attacks and avoid taking damage. Overall though, if you can even partially survive an old top down shooter, you will do fine.  The difficulty varies. Some fights are going to be simple and straight forward (one essentially tells you the next action you should take) while some can be absolutely painful to try and figure out. That said, if jRPGs are nothing new for you, this game will give you some tough battles but never feel unbeatable (so long as you aren't insane.)  So in short: +Well written characters that are either fun to be around or you wish they were around more. +Mercy system is done well and ties into the overall story as well. +No story padding, no grinding. -While the pacifist route is fleshed out a bit, the fighting seems more shallow than a vanillia jRPG, not giving you much of an option to choose it. Overall: Definitely recommend buying it, jRPG fan or not.

It tries to do too much. The outpost system, limiting units, limiting structures and a dumbed down way to upgrade your tech level (ways to unlock more powerful units/turrets) just dont mesh well here. Add to it the minor factions that may or may not be on your map, and its a game that tries too much, and fails.  With limited access to units, you are left with either expanding rapidly, or build turrets to attempt to slowly turtle forward to new outposts. However both methods have major disadvantages.  -Expanding rapidly leads to issues with making the ideal unit comp. With so few units possible to command at one time, you either have to guess at what you will be fighting or move forward with a very generalised comp.   -Crawling foward has the issue of being low on resorces. Since you need to expand to increase income, slowly moving forward leads to being potentially left behind in tech level and unit production. That is an issue because of the limit on turrets per outpost (territory under you control). With only three turrets to defend with, you must (again) guess at what is going to be thrown at you, or generalise.   Ultimatly, the game has interesting ideas but is crippled by the extreemly limiting population caps. [B]Going forth and hoping that your comp will be relivant when you enter combat is never fun. [/B]Add to it the limited locations that you can call units from (you CAN get them to your front line faster, but that has major drawbacks depending on where the front line is), and sending in your few precious units to get instantly destroyed can become extreemly costly.

Clean up the UI, correct the bugs, you'll have a tight game - one I will GLADLY play over again. Keep it in its current state...you have a typical indie game: broken.

Eastshade is one of the loveliest  games I've ever played. The environments are breaktaking, the quests are creatively designed and gel into a fascinating thematic whole, and the ending is one of the most emotionally satisfying I've ever encountered. Level geometry pops in and out of existence unexpectedly, dialogue trees work themselves into invalid states, and the player and their vehicles can get stuck on level geometry in such a way that the only way out is a restart, losing game progress. To name a specific example, I couldn't see or turn to seee the character confronting me at the emotional climax of the story because of a technical issue seemingly related to the bike I was on at the moment the conversation started--nearly ruining an otherwise brilliantly conceived scripted event.  I highly recommend the game anyway. It's an experience unlike any other game out there, and clearly made with an infectious amount of love and creativity. Just... remember to save often.
