Learning my way around the systems and technologies, organizing the elements in my base, and starting to climb the tech tree. It felt like there were so many options to explore and discover. Different avenue of research dried up, while innumerable platform geometries of little difference clogged up by build menu. Things got bigger but no more interesting.  I hit a certain stride once I got resource and soil canisters, and was tractoring huge loads of minerals around, but this was the last time I had fun with the game. Settling new planets had become a highly repetitive chore.  I finished my final goal, building the largest rocket. I realized there was nothing I wanted to do with it, so I just...stopped. I've been left with a bad taste in my mouth, and I won't be recommending this game unless someone asks.

This really shows in the first boss battle which is just a slog to wittle down th bosses health while there is no real threat.  To elaborate on this: Some game mechanics are not well thought out. I compare this game more to the Last King`s Bounty The Legend (I haven`t played any Disciples Games before). In KGTL fights were also easy and one could certainly guess if you could win a fight or not. But it was important to minimize casualties. Here in DL the game uses singular units instead of army stacks. That way it doesn`t matter if your unit is almost dead or at full health. At the end of a fight you just use one of the healing shrines. There is no preassure to play good in the fights. I was able to just brute force my way through, even not taking one of the overpowered mage classes. And if I manage to loose some troops it is really easy to recruit new ones and train them to your level.  Then there is some lost potential with unit abilities and army composition. In theorie there is a good and solid mechanic. Your units have one attack ability with various effects, one special ability with a cool down, most often a passive ability and a back line ability. The back line is a 3 slot system where you can put units which do not activly fight but rovide buffs or debuffs and auto attacks. So there is the potential to mix and match your army for different strategies. But I wasn`t forced to do that. I played with the demon horde as my main army. But I guess it wouldn`t be so different with elves. Yes there are different abilities and preferences (range or melee). But every army has ranged, melee, tanks and so on. The game didn`t require me to think of a special killer combo setup. Also some abilities are clearly better than others even on the same unit Tiers.  Then mst battles will be one with almost no casualties. So there is the option to skip easy fights and well also hard ones. The Coquor ability lets you do this. But if you implement a game mechanic which lets you auto win boring fights doesn`t that show you that there is something clearly wrong with the fundamental game mechanics? The fights are the meat and bone of the game. You work your way up in the Tiers to get new interesting units and you want to use them. Just to see that they are not that special and do not change your gameplay much. Most often higher Tier units are just better and more powerfull. Don`t get me wrong, there are some cool units. The Demon ugraded Succubus which fire arrows and heal your inits for damage dealt are cool.  And if I am speaking of higher Tier units let me say ssomething to the pacing: I am a slow and methodical player. And I don`t skip dialogues. But it took me around 30 hours to finish the 5th map. And the Tier progression is hard locked to finsih this map with the first boss battle. So until this point I was stuck with Tier I and II units. Only after this battle could I use Tier III units. The highest Tier is IV. The Tier III units are cool and more interesting But it was a slog to get there. The pacing is not good. Also the usage of different faction units is tied to a faction standing system. I wasn`t able to manage to get two faction to the required standing to use the Tier III units. Only for one faction. So even mixing two different faction units ist out of the question for at least some more hours.  And soon I realized that using Tier III units is not that much different than T I and T II. Most have more AoE attacks. But fights often gollow the flo of using your cooldown ability whenever ready and only considering using it for maximum AoE effect. The AI uses all abilities as soon as they are ready, not even considering if they double buff the same units, which don`t stack for example. So fights are still boring. You move up, pop your secondary ability and use the rest of the fight your standard attack (which is an ability in of it self, granted. So it has different properties like damage tye and secondary effects.). The fights are most often done before you can use your cooldown ability a second time. There is no real tactics involved: No need to wait for the best moment to pop your cooldown ability. Also the cooldown abilities are often either som esort of damage ability or a heal or buff. More could have been done here. Maybe tone back secondary abilities and only have normal attacks but make them more nuanced and like a signature attack. Incorporate some of the secondary abilities in the normal attacks. If most of the fights you are using the normal attacks anyway. Thst way units of different factions could be more nuanced and factions could be more refined.  Some quick thoughts: Graphics are good, unit design is cool. Albeit a bit glossy. Sound and music is good. Voice acting decent to good. Story writing is mediocre. Some companions are just to eager to join you besides slaughtering their people. It is just ticking boxes, talking to them and triggering secondary quests all at the same time. Also it is a bit strange that you can kill faction armies while at their respective army camo and still talk to their leaders?!? The romance option though are sometime really hillarious and often cringe worthy. Just use them all the time for fun. I mean getting on with an undead werewolf in an afterlife prison is kind of cool?!?  Also most of the spells are useless. Your main character is the only one who can use them. Many level 1 spells are only single target. Why should I buff one unit if I could use another spell which buffs all my units? Or damage a bunch of enemies? Here is a problem with action efficiency. If my spells uses my one atttack action, the spells should be equally important.  In the end even with all the criticism I still had fun but I wont finish the game. I played till shortly after map 5. If you have a lot of spare time and don`t mind an easy game, this isn`t a bad buy. But if your gaming time is limited and you want a good experience I wouldn`t recommend this game.  It feels as if it has this potential to be great, just around the corner, just some hours more. This feeling got my until 35 hours. But not further.

So gute Spiele wie Stranded Alien Dawn erscheinen im Schnitt nur alle 5 Jahre. Ihr seht: ich bin begeistert. Es macht unglaublich viel Spaß auf einem fremden Planeten langsam etwas aufzubauen, damit die Charaktere den vielen Gefahren wie Kälte und Hunger trotzen können. Die nächste Gefahr liegt in den regelmäßig auftretenden Tier/Rudel Angriffen zu trotzen.So muss man also auch etwas für die Verteidigung tun. So baut man zum Schutz immer besser werdende Zäune, Mauern und Wachtürme usw. Bei aller Freude an diesem Spiel möchte ich trotzdem anmerken, dass Verbesserungen braucht. Die häufig auftretenden Nervenzusammenbrüche erscheinen mir reichlich unrealistisch und nervig, besonders unglaubwürdig erscheint mir, dass diese Meltdown-Zustände bestehen bleiben, wenn gerade ein Großangriff auf unsere Basis stattfindet. Ich begrüße dass es jetzt einen Pazifistenmodus gibt in welchem sich die Tiere relativ normal bzw. friedlich verhalten, noch besser wäre ein Szenario in welchem die Tiere durchaus auch mal agressiv reagieren, aber daß mich ein Schwarm von 150 Riesenskorpionen angreift ist einfach unrealistisch und kann für die Charaktere logischerweise letal sein. GAME OVER. Sicherlich wird es viele Spieler geben die gerade diesen brutalen Überlebenskampf lieben. Hier bietet das Spiel viele Möglichkeiten durch Einstellung der Startparameter ein Überleben unwahrscheinlich zu machen. Aber ich bin sicher dass viele Spieler gerade diese harten Voraussetzungen lieben. Sehr viel Spaß macht auch die Möglichkeit der Forschung allgemein sowie die Erforschung der Umgebung mittels Ballon oder ausgedehnte Spaziergänge. Die Charaktere sind gut gelungen in ihrer Unterschiedlichkeit und der Möglichkeit sie durch ständig wiederholte Aufträge in verschieden Bereichen ihre Fähigkeiten auszubauen. So entstehen immer wieder neue Charaktereigenschaften und das gemeinsame Zusammenleben dieser Individuen ist oft lustig, motiviert und die einzelnen Charaktere können einem so ans Herz wachsen. Deswegen schmerzt es mich jedesmal wenn ich ein Grab für ein Gruppenmitglied bauen muss. Ich bin da wohl doch der eher pazifistische Typ. Auf jeden Fall werde ich diese Spiel noch öfter zocken und ich bin gespannt auf die weitere Entwicklung, Updates und neue Inhalte.

I recommend this game for the price I paid for it - $1 as a part of the a Humble Bundle deal.   Hard Reset was supposed to be an homage to the old school FPS games, but there are several design choices that prevent the game from reaching its potential.   The visuals are fantastic and they are by far the best aspect of the game. It played extremely well on a 21:9 ultrawide monitor without any problems, which is great considering this game was released in 2012.   Pretty much everything else is a step back, and could use some improvement.   Soundtrack is a fairly generic, and it ramps up when there are enemies. Enemies don’t seem to make any noise during movement, and I often found myself getting attacked from behind and there was absolutely no sound to indicate that there were enemies flanking.   Weapon system is needlessly complicated. Instead of giving the player a shotgun, rocket launcher etc., the game only has two weapons, a C.L.N weapon and an N.R.G weapon. A shotgun is a weapon mode of C.L.N weapon, and a railgun is a weapon mode of N.R.G weapon. So if the player wants to quickly switch between a shotgun and a railgun, it takes two button presses (equip the N.R.G weapon, and switch to the railgun mode) instead of one, and in the heat of combat, that is enough to get the player killed. There was no need to improve upon the conventional weapon system, the reason begin, it was tried and tested over the years, and this awful system adds nothing but busywork.   The game difficulty primarily comes from large enemy numbers, poor movement mechanics and awful reload/recharge times for weapons. I would be fine with there being a large number of enemies if the movement was smooth and the weapons reloaded at a “normal” rate.  As it stands, this leads to frustration and not fun.   In 2012, there aren’t as many shooters with similar gameplay. In 2018, there are many excellent shooters in this sub genre, such as the Wolfenstein, Doom (2016). Play those first, and if you are still not satiated, then pick up this game for less than $5.   Verdict - Excellent visuals, frustrating gameplay. Pick it up on deep discount.

Even with mods and third party programs, the original Baldur's Gate does not work very well on newer systems at higher resolutions. You can get the game to work well enough with DXwnd but every time you talk to someone the screen will have to scroll to centre the characters in the top left of the screen.  If it wasn't for this, I wouldn't recommend the Enhanced Edition. Instead of just updating the game to run properly on newer systems and adding some quality of life tweaks (they did do this and a good job they have done in this area) they also saw fit to replace and add many things to the detriment of the overall package.  Most critically, like other older methods of updating the game, this release essentially ports Baldur's Gate 1 into the Baldur's Gate 2 engine. This changes some of the core mechanics, changes the spell effects to be a bit more flashy and in general you are not getting the original experience. The changes are not radical, but it's worth keeping that in mind.  Similarly, the new cinematics are not only less numerous than in the original, they also brush over important details found in the original FMVs. The ending cinematic in particular is almost incomprehensible and you'll want to look up the original on youtube once you complete the game as the replacement will leave you absolutely puzzled as to what has happened.  The majority of new content and characters are poorly written and even more poorly voice acted with no option to remove it if you want the vanilla experience. Most of it is easily ignored and I do wonder if it only sticks out to me because I'm so familiar with the original game.  The new UI is uglier and feels like it has had much less love put into it than the vanilla game, tool tips no longer have a nice scroll opening animation and instead you just get a fairly ugly flat scroll texture with text in it. The journal looks unfinished but I will concede that it is better organised in the enhanced edition.  Other graphical changes like sprite outlines, sprite smoothing and character selection circles are painfully ugly and turned on by default. Some people may like these but to have them on by default is going to give some people a very bad first impression, especially people who have played the original game.  ** I recommend turning off sprite outlines and filtering in the graphics options, and in the feedback menu turning on classic character selection circles. This will go a long way to making the game look like it once did. **  A further odd choice is a filter that is placed over the background art, making it look blurrier than it should. Zooming out one click and zooming in actually removes this and it looks much nicer. Clicking the middle mouse button to reset zoom will reintroduce the filter. It's very odd. I found that zooming out three clicks on the scroll wheel resulted in the cleanest look and luckily the game will save your zoom level so it's not a huge deal. [An update allows you to toggle this filter so this paragraph has been rendered moot somewhat.]  For new players there are additional difficulty options to make the game easier which you can ramp up on the fly once you get the hang of things and veteran players will like the higher difficulty modes that are available.  So, in conclusion this is probably the best way to play Baldur's Gate on a modern computer but it will take a bit of digging around in the options menus to get everything to your liking and it is just not as faithful to the original game as I would like. The new content is not very good but can mostly be ignored and in the end, the core of Baldur's Gate is still here, one of the best CRPGs ever made. I wish Beamdog had been more respectful of the original developers intentions when adding content and making changes but the core game still shines through.

[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/6142328/][b] With 1,300+ reviews, make sure to follow The Cpt Froggy Club Curator Page for plenty more![/b][/url][/quote]  Blind Fate: Edo no Yami: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~   The game takes place in the aftermath of the apocalypse in Japan. Your name is Yami, a Demon Hunter, part of the Shogunate. Now a blind cyber-Samurai equipped with a sharp sword in one hand and an arm that can shoot projectiles, you are sent by your master to retrieve information from the Tengun AI. This is Blind Fate: Edo no Yami!  Blind Fate: Edo no Yami is a cyberpunk, hack-and-slash platformer game developed by Troglobytes Games and published by 101XP on the 15th of September 2022 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS4/PS5, Xbox One, Xbox One Series X|S and Nintendo switch.  What an interesting game with interesting ideas and mechanisms, but I don’t think they gel correctly together. In this game, there are 11 locations to visit, including the Dojo, where you can train, receive upgrades for melee and distance weapons, health, stamina and, of course, unlock new skills. To unlock a skill, you’ll need experience points which you gather by eliminating enemies during a level. There are 6 skills in total, and you can upgrade them 4 times. All the other upgrades will be found as data through the levels and can be implemented at the Dojo through Tengo the AI.  As you start the game, you will play the first level until a certain point, and from there, you’ll be able to access the Dojo. From that point, you’ll be able to select any of the available levels that are currently unlocked. You can go back to all unlock levels at any time to try to complete them 100% if you wish. But when you unlock the Palace, you must finish and beat the last boss before returning to the Dojo.   The gameplay is interesting in itself, but the combat mechanisms are my biggest complaint! Yes, the game is a bit challenging at first as you get used to the three senses that Yami has, but as you unlock more skills, the challenging aspect of the game diminishes rapidly. So, what are Yami’s senses? Well, as he is blind, he can’t see the world he is in at first, and he will need to rely on his hearing to locate data, upgrades, lore, medick, and bullet kits which all make noises. As he finds data, the world will appear and also change as he moves further into the level. He also uses his hearing to detect enemies. The heat senses will allow him to find new areas with the levels as long as there is heat. And the last sense can detect lives around the levels. But let’s be really fair here, you will probably use the hearing sense at least 95% of your playthrough. The other aspect of the senses is that they activate the super moves, which I found really fun at first but draining after a while as it slows down the combat dramatically. What do I mean by that? Well, all the ground enemies need to be hit several times, and then a sense symbol will appear next to their life bar. You activate the super move by switching to the correct senses for a few seconds. During these few seconds, the image will be static, except for a beam of white light that shoots onto the image at an angle and becomes narrower as you look at it. In the middle of this light, an orange arrow will appear, and you need to move Yami’s arrow onto the orange arrow and press the attack button to activate the kill. It just slows down the combat fluidity far too much. Not only can you stunt enemies and activate another powerful attack, but this time, you have to press the gamepad buttons in sequences shown during the move to execute it. That said, once you unlock the second, third and fourth stomping skills, not the challenging aspect of the game is gone, and you’ll probably use this move instead of the repetitive slow moves.   The bosses’ fights are fun, but within the first couple of attempts, you’ll definitely figure out how to defeat them (including the last boss), which is a bit of a shame.  In terms of enemies, they are mostly ground robots of different sizes and a couple of aerial robots too. So again, the start of the game is a bit more challenging than after you’ve unlocked some skills.  The story is average, but I did enjoy the artistic cutscenes, which refreshed the game. Graphically, the game is sound, and the apocalyptic atmosphere is well portrayed. The fact that there are too many slow-motion attacks, even if you decide not to follow through with them, negatively impacts the gameplay.   This title has been translated into 10 languages and has full controller support and Steam cloud.   Positives: ~~~~~~~   +	Nice graphics +	Interesting concept with the implementation of senses +	Nice hand-drawn cutscenes +	The ability to come back to any level to complete it +	Achievements  Negatives: ~~~~~~~~   -	Not a very challenging game -	Too many slow-motion attacks -	No trading cards  Blind Fate: Edo no Yami is an interesting concept but has far too many slow-motion attacks, which impacts the fluidity of the combat.    6/10   Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Afterimage is a massive metroidvania and one of the longest and biggest ones out there. It's full of beautiful maps, very free exploration, and a large number of items and upgrades to find. The movement and combat are similar to the Castlevania games, and I found them quite enjoyable.  There are two problems holding this back from being as good as it could've been, though. The first is that the music is rather lacklustre; most of the game's music is completely forgettable, and the Field of Hydro is one of the most surprising and striking areas of the game precisely because it actually has a strong BGM supporting it, so it's a shame the rest of the game doesn't match up.  The other, bigger problem is the translation. It's an obvious ESL job full of grammatical mistakes and awkward phrasing all throughout the game, which is frankly bizarre when they went to the trouble of giving it an English dub. The game's story is extremely convoluted, told in many piecemeal fragments spread throughout the game before culminating in large plot dumps towards the end, but because of how the story is told in combination with the rough translation, it's extremely difficult to follow and understand any more than the bare basics of what's going on in the story.  I can very much recommend Afterimage for the great aesthetics, the exploration, and the combat all being solid, so it's just a shame that a few elements hold it back from being a true masterpiece.

The persistent progression pacing seems awfully grindy. After 5 runs and nearly 5 hours of gameplay time, I've amassed what would have have been enough gold for a second character class had I not spent it on anything else. The other purchase-able class is twice as expensive, and the remaining class is unlocked through a quest I haven't seen yet. The types of things I have purchased- stat boosts, better starting cards, etc.- give the impression that I'm expected to fail multiple times before I'm given the tools to succeed, though I'll concede I did at least reach what I assume is the final boss on my second run (and only that run, so far).  All this might be more palatable were there more content variety from run to run, but the world map seems to have the same 6 areas every time, and each area seems to always have both the same side area and the same boss. There are variations in enemies, equipment, and spells, but these are arguably too minor on a run-to-run basis to justify the amount of repetition needed to meaningfully progress.  Even a single instance of bad card-draw luck can immediately end your run- especially during a boss fight- and yet, if you never push your luck, death by a thousand cuts is a real possibility. Perhaps further unlocks alleviate this, but I personally don't have the patience to find out in this case.  Encountering gear that does not befit your character class in the slightest is not uncommon, nor is finding treasure rooms that only give gold that, apart from the occasional shop or event, is only used for persistent progression once you return to camp. Such instances make runs feel longer than they should. On a related note, I often feel compelled to enter side areas for the extra experience and other rewards, but they seem to lengthen runs beyond what feels merited to me.  There is an elemental affinity system that feels like nothing more than incidental background noise because you have virtually no ability to change your elemental offense and defense on short notice. If an enemy is weak to holy damage, you may incidentally have cards providing that or you may not, so why be concerned about it? Is the system itself even strictly necessary to the game's core design, or is it just extraneous complexity?  I think I may have enjoyed Void Tyrant more without a persistent progression system, and with less acute punishment for bad card-draw luck, but as it stands I'm hesitant to give it a recommendation unless neither criticism fazes you. I do enjoy the core idea of a blackjack / card strategy hybrid, but overall there just seems to be too much baggage holding it back.

PROS:  + Beautifully animated graphics + Anime cutscenes + Fun and addictive gameplay + A welcome return to Metroidvania + Large map + Banging soundtrack  CONS:  X Notably easy, with almost no balance. X No difficulty settings or challenge modes. X Little to find and collect within the labyrinth.  Phil's capsule review: The fifth game in the Shantae series, Seven Sirens drops the hub world select screen of the previous two titles for an interconnected Metroidvania map. The change is good, and the adventure itself is a hair whipping, gem collecting, bikini armor wearing blast. Issues emerge, however, in the realm of balance. About halfway through the game, I was so overpowered and rich with money and health items I was almost invincible. Enjoyment of Seven Sirens may depend on how willing you are to NOT die, and there are no higher difficulty settings or challenge modes. Another problem has to do with what lies within the labyrinth, or rather, what doesn't. Once Shantae is able to fully explore the map, there isn't much worth discovering within it. Still, if you enjoy the Shantae games and have made it up to here, there's no reason not to pick this up.

Jedna z nejpopulárnějších sérií se z Playstationu poprvé podívala na PC a dopadlo to výborně. Sice začínáme od čtvrtého dílu, ale to vůbec ničemu nevadí. Kolekce obsahuje 2 hry: Uncharted 4: A Thief´s End a spin-off Uncharted: The Lost Legacy.    Začněme u Uncharted 4: A Thief´s End.  Původně jsem ke hře přistupoval jako k Tomb Raideru, akorát s rozdílem, že se hraje za chlapa a ne za ženskou. Hlavními tahouny jsou samozřejmě příběh a zajímavé postavy. Jak již bylo zmíněno, tím, že se začíná od čtvrtého dílu, tak mi chyběly určité souvislosti mezi některými událostmi a přiznám se, že jsem občas tápal i co se týče vztahů mezi některými postavami. Naštěstí takových situací bylo pomálu, takže na výsledném hodnocení se nijak zásadně nepodepsaly. Ty nejdůležitější události a motivace hlavních hrdinů jsou ve hře zmíněny a vysvětleny. Za největší slabinu považuji akční pasáže. Byť jsem hrál na gamepadu, tak to nebylo úplně košér (na klávesnici a myši si snad hraní ani nebudu představovat). Druhou výtku mám k renderování shaderů, ke kterému docházelo při každém třetím až čtvrtém spuštění hry.   Ke spin-offu mám ty samé výtky, tady to už díky hraní za ženskou postavu byla jasná alternativa k Tomb Raideru, ale opět velmi zdařilá. Příběh a postavy opět solidní, zasazení a nádherné prostředí Indie také super. Mínus opět za akční pasáže a renderování shaderů (viz výše).  Celkově hodnotím 90%, jelikož se jedná o mé první setkání s touto značkou. Velice rád bych si doplnil vzdělání s původní Drakeovskou trilogií, pakliže vyjde remake jako u The Last of Us: Part 1, tak rozhodně kupuji. Jsem samozřejmě zvědavý, jak to s celou značkou dopadne, protože oba příběhy nechaly otevřené konce. Jestli bude Uncharted 5 s Drakeovou dcerou nebo se opět setkáme s Chloe Frazerovou, tak se rovněž zlobit nebudu.

"This is the single smoothest and most user-friendly digital version of a tabletop game I have ever played.  And it's free to play. Not a big download. If you're remotely interested in tabletop deck-building games then get it and try it. No-brainer.  That said, it's in Alpha as I write, so I'm forewarned of bugs, you must be too. It does occasionally crash (mostly when I click the icon to back out of a decision screen to view the field). But not so often that it's destroying the fun (I've even been able to return to and continue a multiplayer game after a crash, which is a good sign). And I have confidence the bugs will be fixed, since the rest of the experience is just so, so smooth.  This smoothness extends to the tutorial and built-in rules guidance: it's streamlined, it tells you what you need to know to get started and just have fun experimenting.  The game per se, i.e. mechanically, is the archetypal deck-builder. With the market stacks changing each game there's a huge potential variety... once you've got a few different sets in play (i.e. the base game alone won't give you endless replayability). But the base is free and it looks like there's a DLC set unlocked on rotation, so you can get a very good feel for Dominion using the free-to-play game as it stands.  I'd like to see a version of online play in which player timers are more robust. Currently the most immediate style of play is ""30 minutes"" which gives each player a full 30 minutes to play... and no individual turn timer. So I've been left hanging sometimes by a player who just seems to step away from their machine and not come back. I'd have to wait up to 30 minutes in effect for them to time out? Which essentially forces me to quit. A turn-based countdown would keep things moving and not force the attentive player to have to ""concede"" to a player who's gone AWOL."

Primero, tanto Uncharted 4 como The Lost Legacy los jugué en PS4 Pro en su tiempo, y esta saga la sigo desde el primero de PS3 pasando por la Vita incluso. Por eso aunque no lleve muchas horas de juego en esta versión, puedo opinar en base a rendimiento técnico y gráficos ya que en el resto todo ya lo conozco. En cuanto a jugabilidad, es fácil de aprender y de manejo veloz. Nate se mueve muy bien y es cómodo de manejar, que es indispensable en un juego donde en especial en dificultades altas vas a tener que correr, saltar, rodar y apuntar todo rápido y a veces todo junto. Es un plataformas-shooter en tercera persona donde es básico tener un control de PlayStation o Xbox para disfrutarlo, porque en tiroteos o plataformas rápidas un teclado puede hacerte pasar disgustos aunque sea un teclado gamer. Simplemente el juego siempre fue pensado y diseñado con control en la mano. La historia es buena para ser de aventuras, y engancha lo suficiente como para querer seguir. Además los personajes y su carisma con elementales en esta saga de juegos. En ése punto flaquea The Lost Legacy, porque gran parte de la popularidad de estos juegos está en el humor y sarcasmo de Nathan Drake, de quien además depende toda la trama de toda la cronología. Se puede jugar sin haber jugado los 3 antiguos de PS3, pero al menos lee un resumen de lo que pasó en ellos porque si no, no va a tener gracia y te sentirás como que llegaste a la mitad de la película. Lamentablemente no ha salido la colección clásica en PC, pero si puedes jugarlos de alguna forma, ve de cabeza a jugarlos ya que el mejor incluso que éste al menos para mí es Uncharted 2. De duración Uncharted 4 es un juego promedio de 12 horas, pero depende de tu habilidad, dificultad que elegiste y si buscas todos los tesoros. Con eso podrías acumular unas 30-35 horas en sacar el 100% de ambos juegos, con dificultad máxima que es capaz de hacerte más de un quebradero de cabeza en escenas concretas. The Lost Legacy es un extra que completo dura menos de la mitad que el juego principal, que aunque no está mal, lo veo más como un DLC que como un juego aparte. Es muy corto y simple para ser algo más. Finalmente está lo técnico. Se demoraron mucho en el port, pero el estudio original de desarrollo (Naughty Dog) se destaca por hacer magia con consolas de hardware limitado como era el PS4, por lo que el estudio responsable del port tuvo una buena base. Hay a veces objetos que en primer plano se ven feos cuando contrastan con los paisajes que están muy bien hechos. No tiene mucha variedad de ajustes, pero sí los necesarios para que puedas configurarlo y hacerlo rendir bien con hardware normal de este tiempo. Por lo menos en mi caso Spiderman hizo sufrir mi PC con las temperaturas, pero Uncharted funciona sin problemas a menos que se le suba al extremo el escalado de texturas. Con la primera escena en el mar se notará inmediatamente. Si corres bien esa parte, entonces todo funcionará perfecto. En mi caso subí demasiado las texturas a un nivel ridículo y boté el juego en esa parte, pero sirve como referencia: si tu configuración es estable de FPS en esa parte que tiene mucho efecto y movimientos, entonces todo bien. Si no, bájale la exigencia al escalado, texturado o sombras y seguro te corre bien. Aunque ya lleve sus años el juego original, fue lo suficientemente bien hecho como para que un port a PC se vea genial aunque no sea lo máximo actualmente. Resumiendo, recomendado sobre todo si conoces los de PS3 y nunca pudiste finalizar la historia. The Lost Legacy es un buen añadido, pero no esperes tampoco gran cosa de ésa parte. Y ésa se juega después que el 4, al revés te comerías un spoiler.

This game had me rolling with laughter. Some of the strategies it makes you come up with are really interesting, and a few of the levels are actually quite challenging. Unlike Total War you cant actually tell the troops what to do, so you just sort of place them and hope. Which is honestly far more enjoyable. You essentially set up the battle with the set 'funds' it gives you to buy troops and then press start. Its a much lower risk game that a traditional battle simulator as you dont stay with a consistent starting troop, and theres no penalty for a loss. It basically lets you make the craziest ideas and then test them out. It's definitely a casual pick up and go. Theres no hard commitments, and it can be stopped and restarted/paused at any time.   I have experiences a few bugs, but they are not game breaking. Such bugs have been eyeballs on the wrong place of the face, a mammoth stomping the ground and making dust during planning phase where it should be still, and a berserker getting stuck in a wall.  Ultimately if you like the idea of sending a giant mammoth with googly eyes out into the battle field with like 8 healing mages to combat like 20 knights and watching it all play out, then this game is for you.   10/10 would send google eyes mammoths, gunslingers, dead eyes, and healing mages into battle to fight yarls again.

Full disclosure, I used the fan patch 1.3 and came into this game with a lot of people talking about how bad it is. As with most hype bandwagons, once it gets you expecting too much of something, it kinda feels underwhelming when you actually experience it. So I can say Daikatana didn't feel as bad as most people made it out to be.  Levels are descent, with enough variance between each once as you start going from time period to time period. As well as each period has its own set of weapons being a nice touch. The music is also good, not that memorable, but it doesn't make it harder to sit through the gameplay. Not only that, but the game is short, clocking under 20  hours with some time spent lost and exploring.  But when it comes to the rest of the game it falls apart. The companions are a nice idea, but clearly, the IA at the time wasn't far enough to make it work. I didn't have much problem with them dying, but having them get stuck somewhere and then having to babysit them back to the end of the level wasn't exactly a fun time. The leveling system wasn't bad, but it felt like it barely mattered, the only thing that made any noticeable impact being the Daikatana, but even then it becomes apparent using guns is more efficient.  The story wasn't bad, in fact, it was actually nice seeing the writers trying to push for a more involved narrative in shooters. But each time period felt disconnected from the last, you could almost completely cut out every part between the first and the last level and things would still make enough sense. And while the graphics look good enough for the time, seeing the models stuck to their default position during cutscenes like they're holding something was a bit strange.  Outside of that, there were some technical difficulties with the game, like the intro movie not playing when launching the game and some of the in-game cutscenes skipping themselves. But I believe that could be something on my setup and being part of playing older ports on modern systems.  In all, I can't recommend it as the fun parts found here can be found elsewhere with the better overall quality. You probably could take some fun out of it during sales, but outside of that, it's a hard sell.

On retrouve également les scènes épiques des épisodes passés grâce aux missions variées (infiltration, approche discrète et même parfois des objectifs à atteindre avec furtivité). On regretterait presque la libération de New-york en hélico d'attaque dans MW3, ou la course poursuite dans les favelas de MW2.  Pour ce qui est du multijoueur, on retrouve le cocktail ayant fait les beaux jours de la franchise : beaucoup de bienveillance, du fair-play à la louche et surtout du beau jeu grâce à une communauté qui se préoccupe - entre autres qualités - bien plus de l'atteinte de l'objectif en équipe que du ratio K/D. AI + Half the price of a triple A game but definitely with the presentation of a triple A game makes up for the shorter gameplay + Fancy keyboard lighting that fit's the style of the game + Great checkpoint system that prevents too much repetition  Cons - The game only saves between each level (not between each checkpoint). If you don't know this and you leave the game mid level, you lose a lot of progression. - RTX makes a huge drop on the FPS, more that I noticed for instance in Control. NOTE: WAIT FOR PERFORMANCE PATCHES OR A SALE BEFORE ACTUALLY BUYING IT. LOTS OF PEOPLE ARE REPORTING OPTIMIZATION ISSUES. I PUSHED THROUGH THE AT TIMES MEGA JANK PERFORMANCE BECAUSE I'M A MASSIVE ARKANE SHILL.  With that out of the way Deathloop is pretty baller. The premise is one that's not entirely new (majora's mask, sexy brutale, etc.) but the way its done here is certainly well constructed and interesting. Even though I was playing through the same areas over and over, it was tough to get bored of them as you're always uncovering more and more with new sections of each map either being discovered or re-contextualized. In short, the maps feel like several dishonoured ones crammed together, with interiors reminiscent of how Prey does stuff with different entry points locked by specific abilities, while also having the macro-scale interactivity of things done on one map at a specific time affecting what can happen later on in a loop. Not to mention that by the time you ARE just running through a zone to get something done, the game gives you the tools to just sanic your way through it so you're not slogging through the zone again.  The powers, while initially seemingly just ripped right out of dishonoured which worried me at first, get more and more interesting as the game progresses. Which honestly seems to be a theme with the rest of the game: it starts out feeling somewhat rote but the more you dive in the crazier it gets.   Story-wise. It's Arkane studios. It's pretty good but as usual I found the actual plot to take a backseat to the worldbuilding and characters. The time loop could have been a plot to steal the world's gumball supply or whatever and it wouldn't really matter to me.   All in all. Loved it, will probably come back later down the line when this thing is optimized.

[h1]I want to give Fatshark the thumbs up, but I just can’t[/h1]  Darktide in a lot of ways is a project of real passion. The music is undeniably amazing in this game and easily trumps a lot of what I’ve heard in other titles with its creativity. Many missions have insane levels of detail and a sense of scale captured in the most jaw dropping way.  The core game loop is fun and has decent replayability.  However, the game has some issues. Awful performance, lack of class diversity, missing crafting systems, non paid cosmetic variety and no presence of endgame. In the pre-release beta, I overlooked a lot of these problems because I felt that Darktide was honestly enjoyable to me. I had confidence in Fatshark’s commitment to the game since the closed beta and I still do. In time the game can only get better. It’s the choices made by the developers right now that are concerning me.  The cash shop being the first and functional feature available at launch is a slap in the face. On top of it all, the community has already pointed out its predatory nature. This isn’t a new practice, but given just how bad performance is and the missing features promised in the release version, it’s just wrong of Fatshark to have the ingame shop come out on launch.   I really want to support this game, but I don’t want to support the choices being made right now. I have no problem with there being a cosmetic shop in a more stable and feature rich title, but Darktide is not that at this moment. This practice with early access titles is becoming obnoxious and it needs to stop.

I really wanted to like this game. Many game mechanics are esoteric. The only way to learn is by screwing up and trying to reload. But reloading reloads the game in an alternate state with units disappearing, and the Ai is able to move before your screen loads fully. Territory shapes make a mockery of district adjacency planning. Strategic resources needed by cultures like Egypt are never accessible in the amount and combination you need them due to a scarcity bias. Start location can make or break games on higher difficulty. In the neolithic era, curiosities sometimes DO NOT spawn near you for the first five turns, or more depending on your path, which means you are assigned bottom tier cultures. Only some cultures are competitive. The main way to win the game is by snowballing, which means it stops being fun early and the rest of the game is just grinding. With enough science in the final eras, you won't have enough time or maybe production to build units and buildings you unlock. This leads to games where your science lead is so bananas that what you build and what your units do on the map has no bearing on whether you win the game. Combat is insane. With the simple example of a nomad tribal unit and a bear, sometimes moving from one tile to another makes the difference between the bear doing 10 damage versus 50 damage. There are no shifts of either unit to/from a river or an elevated tile, and there's no other unit adjacencies I can discover that should account for such a crazy difference in the combat rolls. Archers take a penalty from units in front of them but can shoot over mountains. The list goes on. It's only after playing for 100 hours that I'm voting this game down. Others love this game. I really wanted to.

There is a realm of politics, military and economy that all really mesh together well. It reminds me of the super fun board game and I'm happy they took some inspiration mechanics wise from it. I enjoyed levying debuffs on specific factions, getting buffs on myself, going for positions on the council and more.  The factions have plenty of unique flavor to them, allowing you to really enjoy a unique playstyle depending on who you play.  The game runs surprisingly smooth for launch. Never crashed or had any issues, just a stutter every hour or so... and that's only around a second. Painless.  First match on medium ~3-3.5 hours. You could probably rush it faster.  The cons: No multiplayer yet, but they already acknowledged they wanted to add it. Seems they are launching single player to focus on core game bugs, etc.  No tutorial really. The game throws hints at you but it does take a little bit to grasp what's going on. That being said, with some patience you can figure it out pretty quickly as the interface is pretty easy to use.  Some quests can be a bit vague / not straight forward. I didn't understand what it meant by spy operation first until I dug around a bunch (I thought it was spying on the factions, not actually using abilities). I hope some in line clickable links on quests are added to take you where the objectives of a quest are.   The unknown: Replayability. I'll edit this post on the replayabilty of the map as I'm unsure if everything is hardset or not. I'd guess they rotate spice deposits and allies ofc.  Overall... I'm incredibly happy with the game and I think Shiro nailed it off the bat. Looking forward to seeing how they update the game and add more factions / features / etc.

This so barely gets a positive review and this is why.   I always wanted to play it. As a kid, this game was the biggest curiosity for me. Interactive movies weren't a thing really then and so this caught my eye. Finally it's on PC and... wow, what a mess of a game.   The port is so bad that literally the emulator runs this shit better. Every time I loaded into a new area on an SSD, the game would have these insane freezes. I had to let the game only access 3 out of the 8 cores to reduce the stutters. I also had to turn the game to 30fps, which was a terrible 30fps as well with awful frametimes.  I liked the characters and they were interesting in general. Likeable, at least.   The story itself was too long and it's bad crime fiction. The answers are made up and the players can't take part in really speculating and analyzing the information presented to them since most of the time the game presents completely random people as suspects. It's watching people react after solving their crimes, not people actually solving a crime.   Don't worry, no spoilers. But just saying, the conclusion is bad. The worst I've seen in any crime fiction. Why? Because it's literally impossible. Like it's literally impossible. Nothing fits and nothing makes sense. It's literally, as in physically, impossible. This is not a game about magic and stuff, so that doesn't explain it either. It's just flat out impossible.   Overall I'm glad I was allowed the opportunity to finally play this and for that it gets the thumbs up. The price during sales is reasonable and at the end of the day I was one of the people begging for this game. But also if you're just stumbling on this game thinking it might be good, it won't. It's comically bad at best, but the comedy ends when instead of seeing like the most excessive amount of interactive urination you'll ever see turns into actual arrogance on the writer's behalf.   So yeah... were you desperate to play it like me? Go and get your slap in the face for thinking it might just be so bad it's funny, rather than being a baffling case of incompetent writing that brags how clever it is.

Jedes Spiel bietet eine für die Zeit reiche und interessante Spielwelt. Die Schwächen der Hauptstory im zweiten und dritten Teil, die aus meiner Sicht vor allem durch die Reihenfolge der Spiele und damit einhergehenden Inkonsistenz von Entscheidungen und Geschichte, werden durch interessante Gefährten und ihren persönlichen Storys ausgeglichen. In Retrospektive gefällt mir die Story des ersten Teils am besten, auch wenn den Gefährten ein bisschen Tiefe fehlt. Einzelne Gameplayelemente wie der Mako im ersten Teil sind selbst in der Legendary Edition noch sehr clonky und auf Dauer nervig. Insgesamt lohnt sich die Legendary Edition allerdings trotzdem für gute 120 Spielstunden, einige philosophische Diskussion mit Freunden, die es spielen oder gespielt haben und für einige (viele) Lacher durch Dialoge oder Shepards Gesichtsausdruck. Mit der Mass Effect Legendary Edition kann man nichts falsch machen, erst Recht nicht, wenn man bis dahin nie Mass Effect gespielt hat.

The turning radius on most vehicles is pure garbage and learning to drift or point turn will not change the fact that the turning radius is simply too wide for any car. The microtransaction demon has reared its ugly head again with this game and it's downright predatory. You're already paying full price for the game, we don't want a battlepass for this game too. The battlepass is garbage. There isn't enough there to warrant paying $40 US for 550 in-game currency and one vehicle. The Speed Champion cars, outside of the Tutorial, are not found anywhere. Overall a fun experience, but I would wait to get this game if I had the choice to buy it again. Hope this helps!

Después de haberlo platinado y siendo este el primer juego del género Soul q juego tengo q decir que es un obra maestra.  Es un juego que te enseña muchas lecciones y aprendes muchas cosas por las buenas o por las malas. Dark Souls te lleva constantemente a replantearte todo, como pelear, que estrategia usar, prestar atención a TODO lo q te dicen, analizar cosas que podes no estar dándote cuenta, etc. Todo tiene sus reglas y mecánicas.  A esto lo acompaña que no tiene dificultad, con lo cual si te parece dificil como todos sabemos, arreglate... hasta q le puedas encontrar la vuelta, lo cual me parece genial pero por momentos desesperante, aunque es  la esencia del juego, la superación, no hay nada más gratificante que poder superar ese jefe o zona q no podías antes o te volvía loco. La frutilla del postre es la historia, el LORE q tiene hermano, es una completa locura. Es de esas historias atrapantes q tenes q ir atando cabos y sacando conclusiones con las pistas q te van dando en el juego mismo, porque TODO tiene lore, desde los items, hasta las zonas, jefes y cinemáticas, todo se explica minuciosamente.  Sinceramente, pienso q si te encantan los videojuegos como a mi, si o si tenes q jugar a todos los Dark Souls, es tremenda experiencia, algo q tenes q hacer por lo menos una vez en tu vida.

8.5/10. Definitely a must play. One of the best RPG games ever for sure, for a price this low it's a steal for 200 hours+ content.  Story is well written in general but there aren't exactly any plot twists, everything pretty much ends up happening the way you'd expect. Decisions that effect how the game ends are ridiculous also. However, it has very fun quests, best one is in the main storyline so you won't miss it, I never laughed that hard in a video game before, writers sense of humor is just perfect.  [b]Very important tip:[/b] It has the worst quest tracking system possible for an open world RPG. It's fixable with the mod called `All Quest Objectives on Map`, go get on nexus mods right away before you start the game. It's the biggest quality of life upgrade you can have for this game. But this is one of the major flaws for 8.5 on my side, they never should've released the game like this in the first place while even a mod can fix it that easily.  There are also mods for fast travel from anywhere and unlimited inventory. They would definitely make your life easier but I didn't find those to be that big problems and wanted to avoid mod crashes so I didn't use them.

[h1]Five Dates[/h1]  Really hard to describe if you haven't played it yet, but in the end it turned out to be one of the most interesting games I've played in the last few years. If you like the genre then it is definitely a must play and certainly one of the good FMV games that have made a stunning comeback in that past 7-8 years. The most interesting thing about Five Dates is certainly the main theme and its setting. Because some might have noticed that we have a pandemic and the game wouldn't have made any sense 5 years ago and hopefully 10 years from now it wouldn't make much sense when people play it. It gets to the point without intruding on the subject and without pushing itself into the foreground. It's just there in a very casual way and that's just a fantastic effort in my mind.  So the main topic is the dating. Obviously. And the target group are regular men i guess, but maybe there will be a second part where you can date men as a woman. And that doesn't mean that only regular men should play the game. Just to be sure. You're a guy named Vinny. A regular guy I would say, in his mid-20s, who comes to video-dating because of the lockdown. Getting some tipps and feedback from his best buddy Callum. Both with some outstanding acting and diolouge. There are five girls to choose from and I really think there is something for everyone. Well, they have their parts to play, but again, the acting is superb for a game like this. And having been in a relationship for 10 years now and already having a 7 year old child, I am extremely surprised at how accurate my match was at the end of my first (blind) playthrough. That she ended up being nearly exactly my type. It was Maya with Shaina ending up in a close second. But all five offer some great depth and great character.  [b]Pros:[/b]  +Amazing acting. +Akward, but on point setting that would not be conceivable in any other time like this. +The dialogue, especially Vinny and Callum's, are great. Also most of the dating dialogue. There are over 700 scenes to watch and some of them are hilarious.  +Although I thought there would be a lot of awkward moments and decisions, this part was actually well executed. While there are some weird moments, it never really forces anything on you. It manages to keep it very simple and natural. +At times the game may feel a little flat but there is so much depth going on and some of the themes the game tackles are just wonderful and interesting. There is so much more than meets the eye. +The technical side of the game is perfect. Editing, camera, sound, lighting conditions. And some very helpful subtitles for non-native speakers and those with hearing difficulties.  [b]Cons:[/b]  A playthrough is very short. About 1.5 hours at most and about 6 hours for all the achievements. And other than successfully, or unsuccessfully, meeting all five girls and seeing the endings, there's not much replay value. I am fine with that if i get quality content, but others might not.  [b]Conclusion:[/b]  A must buy for people who like the gerne and a good first game for people who wanna get into it. It shows all the possibilities that full motion video games have to offer and why it is one of the most interesting genres. And the technical part is top-notch. Buy it now or never. Or in the next pandemic.  [b]Personal Score: 8.5/10[/b]

UPD для номинации: На дворе конец 2022 года, игра наконец расцвела и получила преданную фанатскую базу. Серверов уйма, модов ещё больше. Но транспорт так и остаётся больной темой. Даже после выхода патча 1.19 :)))  Начну издалека. С DayZ mod лично у меня связано очень многое. Это единственная игра в которой количество фана, адреналина, веселья, атмосферы, обиды, жалости, чувства кидалова и многого другого просто зашкаливает. Да что там, это единственная игра в которой количество часов проведённых в ней перевалило за 1000! Играл в мод примерно с самого релиза и игра была просто феноменальна, но время шло... появлялись читеры, потом с упадком цены на арму или скидки на распродаже, появились школьники и играть стало невыносимо! Да и целей в моде уже никаких небыло. Появился > налутал топ вещи > начал воевать > убили и всё опять сначала. Кое как ситуацию начали выправлять моды Origins и Epoch, но и там в конечном итоге всё сходилось знакомой схеме. Многие механики попросту не работали, а баги АРМА2 давали о себе знать. И тут выходит DayZ SA. Да, игра в статусе альфы, да многого на момент написания обзора нет. НО! Игра регулярно обновляется, игра постоянно переносит на себе ряд изменений как косметических, так и механических. На 04.08.2014 виден большой прогресс по сравнению с первой версией игры. Уже имеются палатки (можно делать базу), а в период октябрь - декабрь будет добавлен транспорт. Единственно, что пока огорчает, так это зомби... но их в скором времени пофиксят. В SA в отличии от мода нужно выживать, а не тупо стрелять. Есть множество инфекций, болезней, в общем много того, что нужно держать в голове для того чтобы выжить и всё это напрямую влияет на геймплей.  В общем теперь коротко плюсы и минусы:  Плюсы:  - улучшенная оптимизация по сравнению с модом.  - множество улучшений косаемо персонажа, крафта, графики и т.д.  - регулярные обновления - цена (для меня плюс т.к. не каждый школьник сможет выпросить у мамки целый косарь на игру) из этого следует то, что неадекватов в игре будет значительно меньше.  Минусы:  - спавн зомби - немногочисленные баги - отсутствие транспорта (но это временно).  В общем это настоящий Must Have для любителей симуляторов выживания в постапокалипсисе (зомби-апокалипсисе).

It's free and will assist you to reaching a high rank in whatever FPS you want. Use the appropriate exercises (try the recommended exercises from pros and streamers) for a couple weeks straight with ~1-2 hour of training before playing and your aim will assist you in gaining the top ranks. I only have 20 hours because I idle.  I could barely hit bots many years ago and have progressively improve just by playing FPS games. However, I solo queued to diamond (Apex Legends) in just a couple weeks by using the above training method. Remember, these trainers are to assist you in warming up above all else. Positioning, teamwork, etc. are what truly matter. You don't focus on aiming at high elos; aiming should be second nature. It's inefficient to spend your concentration on clicking on another player, when you should be assessing your next move (whether it be retreating, advancing, or holding). I no longer use aim trainer and my aim is still solid. I believe further investment would still be beneficial, but if I were to be more competitive again I would suggest training your aim where it is acceptable to win duels are high elos. Don't fixate and waste time on aim trainers to improve - unless you have the time to be a professional. For us competitive players who have jobs outside gaming, utilize your time recording and analyzing your own game play. You may even find ways to improve your aim by watching how you over-flick, etc. I can partly attribute my diamond to aim, but mostly from learning and being open to my mistakes. Good luck!

This game has charm and detail. Everything feels like it has more of that rough indie charm. Yet after playing it for a fair amount of time (32 hours at time of this review) it shows to have a great amount of depth and detail. Enough that I am currently paused in game to come write this review as I hit a particular moment in this game where I realized I actually care for this land, The bonds I had built up, what I had explored and worked for. In a word 'immersed'. It isn't without flaws. Some balance issues, Voice acting I thought was charming but was a bit rough, SFX will get grating fast, and I found setting up pre fights a slog. Still over all this is well worth the price tag and I am looking forward to next game and even a re-visit.  For those looking for a slightly greater bit of detail on the previous points I will go into more detail here. The voice acting I personally did enjoy. However, It feels slightly off as the dialogue doesn't come across natural. Very much they are speaking information at you rather than it being a conversation. The Voice actors themselves are fun! I still haven't decided if General Vargas has a bad ass voice or a silly one and I love it. While we are in the auditory department the Sound effects balancing will need to be adjusted. Many of the noises quickly become grating (I'm looking at you Rad counter).   Gameplay it was very impressive how much I was able to interact with this world. There are checks for skills all around constantly giving me little endorphin pings for skills I had while simultaneously making me question my builds every time a bomb blew up in my face or I paid full price for ammo. Conversations were also excellent in this game. I would honestly feel a person out before making a speech check. They might react worse to a kiss ass than an asshole. You will find your glibness doesn't always do you credit. Makes them feel like people. Balance feels good around having a big squad. I didn't feel like I had any wasted space and skills. Weapon balance isn't quite as good. I managed so I won't tell you don't use X or Y, but I think it clear the creators loved AR's the most.    I hope this helped at least one of you make the choice whether this game is right for you. If it is well I look forward to seeing you again in the wastes.

While I understand the huge criticisms behind KT's business practices regarding the franchise post-DoA5, DoA6 is surprisingly accessible. Think about it this way: the base game is free with 4 characters, and all of the other characters are free to try with their frame data and combo trials available in-game. This means that you can focus solely on investing in your main. At this day and age where online fighting game communities are becoming ever-so prevalent, the average player needs to invest approximately 5 bucks to get started; if you feel like maining one of the core fighters, you're technically a f2p player. Aside from the season pass costumes, DoA6 has a fair variety in its customization options, with characters like Kasumi having up to 18 in-game non-DLC costumes as well as additional hairstyles and accessories to mix and match with.   That said, the game itself is pretty good--character attacks feel like they have a bit more weight compared to most of the other games out there (even Tekken to some extent due to how they handle knockback, sound design, and distracting block/hit effects).  lol who plays a fighting game for the story anyway

Beyond that there have been a few glitches with mobs and textures but I feel like that is to be expected at this stage so close to launch.   In conclusion, I would certainly recommend the game based on the atmosphere and building systems alone. I see a huge amount of potential for additional content and based on the dev's post-launch statement they seem like they will actually stay on top of it. The game has a similar feel to Valheim in its early days (which depending on your perspective could be either meh or fucking awesome), so if that's cool with you then buy it now. If you want some more polish probably hold off for a few patches, or the first major update before diving in.

It's a smaller romance novel so understandably there are only 3 characters you can date, but that's okay, they're all wonderful! I went with Jonas for that perfect himbo energy; the dialogue is cute and wholesome all the time.   Making potions is also super easy and relaxing! The orders are easy to read/understand and easy to make. The designs for all of the finished items are so, so cool, and it makes me want to have them in real life! Those bottles are so cool. The one thing I did miss out on was getting all the crystals from Ramsey, the best bird, and I do think I might swing back into the game to try and wrangle more achievements out.   The garden is cute, too! That's where ingredients are sourced from. The flowers are cute and they make me happy to see.   There is one thing I do recommend for anyone looking to dive in: make sure you talk to everyone at least once a day! I kind of forgot it was a requirement to get all their special recipe info and then had to use the lovely guides on here to figure it out. Other than that, the playthrough I had was smooth, chill, and fun!   If you're looking for something relaxing and wholesome to ease you into a calm night or day, this is the game for you. 100/10 Pumpkins.

A cleverly-planned, worthy successor in the To The Moon stories. It's both everything you expect and nothing you expect. The music is on point, as Kan Gao always is, with some leitmotifs that echo IF's predecessors in all the right ways. The art style hasn't changed, though movement has improved (we can RUN now!) and what gameplay there was has been further condensed to focus on the narrative. And the narrative is classic Kan Gao. I think To The Moon hit harder, but not by much, and I liked IF more than Finding Paradise. Have a box of tissues ready.   It was worth the wait, and absolutely worth the full price - but despite what the description says, I'd recommend playing at least To the Moon and Finding Paradise first. Preferably also the free minisodes. Since each game/episode is so short (<1hr for the minisodes, 3-4 hrs for the 3 games), you could binge it all in a weekend. Just remember to bring tissues.

Considering you can get this game really cheap, I'm going to give this a tentative reccomend but the game does have its fair share its issues.  First of all, the positives: for the most part I would say the combat is improved. Bigger variety of combos, and different useable weapons. Some enemies are just not fun to fight though.  The level design is also shockingly really good in some places. There are some crazy sections you have to get through. But there is a fair bit of jank and moments of frustration.  The plot is kind of interesting. I like the angle of the prince being a more self-interested and selfish person given his circumstances. They are a bit over the top with the tone though - the prince's constant remarks about the enemies about to meet their demise and the generic henchman lines from the enemies. Along with the cheesy rock battle theme the game is just trying way too hard to be edgy and cool. At least it's got more personality than the half-baked retread of Two Thrones though.  Okay those are the (mostly) positives. Now for the bad stuff.  Touched on this already, but this game is pretty buggy. Along with some glitches that can get you killed for no good reason, there is one *really* bad game-breaking bug you can't really seem to plan for. And one that you shouldn't have to, really. For some reason, the portal to the last boss at the end of the game sometimes does not function and thus you can't beat the game. Reloading the save does not work. You might just be fucked.  My 'solution' was just to reload a much earlier save and play all the way through to the end and hope it was fixed on that attempt. Fortunately that worked but I lost a lot of progress. Apparently this issue is more likely to happen if you travel between the past and present a lot - so I guess try to limit the amount of times you do that. Try not to get too lost in this game - which may be difficult as the more open design of this game compared to the original may have you wandering around a lot without it being entirely clear where you need to go.  Also I have to say this game just hasn't aged as well graphically as the first game. I like the moody and dark aesthetic, but the first game has a more simple and cohesive graphical style.  So yeah, this is a game of high highs with some of the best platforming/parkour moments in the series, but it's also the jankiest of a fairly janky series. The more open design of the world compared to the others is cool, but it's a double-edged sword as you might end up a bit lost or worse - you might end up softlocking your save. So save as often as possible. Or be prepared to not finish the game at all.

This is a pretty great Chapter pack, with some decent perks, and as to be expected with other Chapter packs, new maps, new characters, and a new killer. You have Leon and Jill for Survivors, and Nemesis for Killers. Leon has 2 outfits that you can purchase via microtransactions, his bomber jacket outfit from RE4, and a full model replacement outfit, Chris Redfield (RE5 face and hair on his RE1 outfit). Jill has 2 outfits that you can purchase as well, her blue dress outfit from RE3, and a full model replacement outfit, Claire Redfield (RE2 Remake model). The outfits for Leon are pretty good, but Jill's Claire outfit is really off to me, Claire's model just looks weird for some reason, her model has a really weak chin and it makes her face look pretty ugly from side angles. Nemesis has no outfits, which is a bummer because they could've made Mr. X as an outfit or even the T-002 Tyrant from RE1. The new perks for both Leon and Jill are decent, nothing amazing but they aren't terrible. Nemesis is fun to play as, and to go up against as a Survivor. The new map for this Chapter pack is taken out of the map rotation pool due to issues and crashes, so as of writing this review, you still cannot play the RPD map and I have not been able to play it myself. Apparently the RE4 outfit for Leon and RE3 outfit for Jill were able to have their pieces bought separately, but then the devs changed it to where you had to buy the whole outfit instead of certain pieces, which I think is pretty stupid considering the RE4 Leon head just has slightly longer and more blond hair, and the RE3 Jill head is literally the same head that is used on the default Jill outfit, no changes to it or anything. Overall, this Chapter pack is pretty cool, but with the issues it has and the fact that the map released with this pack is still taken out of the game, this pack should've been cheaper.

I have never been a homeless person. Playing this game would have you introduced to things that you might face as a homeless person. Some of those things may have already known or predicted by you, some may not. I do believe though that the hardships offered inside this game is not the same as actually living such hardships, I suggest you to not accept this game as a simulation. Accept this game as a game that introduces you to potential hardships that you have to face if you were a homeless person.  Overall, it was not a great experience, playing this, A Homeless Survival Experience. Great job for the developer. It was nice to know about things that could happen if I was a homeless person. And what options, that I have, to respond to every day events. There is no excitement for me, no adrenaline rush like surviving from a dinosaur or the joy of building home like playing ARK, just pure struggling to get by. In game, struggling hopefully my situation will get better. There's little that I can plan... as a homeless person.  Also, to me, the time I have for each day as a person inside this game was so short. I do not know if that was intentional. Maybe telling you that each day would feel fast but you don't really have a lot of things to do, as a homeless person.  I recommend this game for introducing a fresh perspective about a topic I'm in concern with. Still, even within that light, I'd like to refund the product.

SpaceChem is love. SpaceChem is life.  This game is about using your programming skills to create [b]space chem[/b]icals using waldos. This might sound simple on paper, but you're wrong. Very, very wrong. Because of two things: 1. You only have limited space in a reactor, [u]80 tiles[/u] 2. The programming language is [u]in that space[/u] and is executed as your waldo moves along the symbols. This gives SpaceChem a very interesting challenge: how do you construct reagents with just this limited scope? And that challenge is just scratching the surface. You can only go over a specific tile twice: once horizontally, once vertically. You NEED to take advantage of this to do anything complex. Let's say you have N₂ with a single bond, and you want it to have a triple bond. What you do is drop it onto some bonders through a grab/drop horizontally, perform two bond + instructions, and then grab it vertically from the same tile of the grab/drop. Now you're holding a triple bond N₂. Fantastic.  Then the game drops a bombshell: fusion. Now you're performing addition with atoms. You can make almost anything as long as you have enough input reagents. Sikutar will break you. Then the game drops another bombshell: flip-flops. Now you can make loops, counters, etc. Remember going over a specific tile twice for specific things? It's now (mostly) a thing of the past! Just go over it again with flip flops. Amazing! Then the game drops another bombshell when you access ResearchNET: fission. Now you're doing ADVANCED math with atoms. You WILL need to bring up a notepad to figure out most nuclear puzzles. Absolutely bonkers.  You'll tear your hair out trying out some of the later puzzles, and rage quit, but then you'll be dreaming about atoms and possible optimizations... Just know you most likely won't be seeing the ending. It is a very hard game after all. And that's okay.

Dagon - это не совсем игра в привычном понимании. Это скорее визуализация одноимённого рассказа небезызвестного писателя в жанре ужасов и вдохновителя 90% разработчиков инди-хорроров Говарда Филлипса Лавкрафта без особого геймплея - что-то типа визуальной новеллы, если искать аналогии в играх, но только в 3D и лишь с монологом главного героя( очень атмосферно озвученным, кстати) вместо диалогов. И в своём, так сказать, жанре, игра показывает себя прекрасно: здесь и хорошая, хоть и видно, что достаточно бюджетная, визуальная составляющая, и отличная озвучка монолога главного героя, и хороший звук в сопровождении атмосферного эмбиента, а также интересные секреты с фактами о творчестве Лавкрафта и о том, что из реального мира на него повлияло. Ну и, конечно же, нельзя упомянуть, что проект полностью бесплатный - вы можете поддержать разработчиков покупкой DLC(или предшествующего Dagon симулятора рыбалки от них, лол), но без них из игры ничего не убудет, и вы всё равно получите полноценный опыт от проекта.  У Dagon, конечно, есть пара недостатков, а именно малая продолжительность(что также можно отнести и к преимуществам, если вы - человек занятой), виновник которой, правда, сам Лавкрафт, потока сознания которого хватило в своё время лишь на такой вот рассказ на полчаса спокойного чтения, и, что уже ничем не оправдаешь, небольшие баги с освещением, когда оно в некоторых местах, как бы сказать, квадратится. В остальном проект отличный и прекрасно дополняющий творчество Лавкрафта - его рассказам с кучей, по его словам, не поддающихся описанию вещей порой крайне не хватает визуализации, чтобы читатель смог полностью ощутить величие существ со дна океана и всего остального, что он там напридумывал невероятного и необъяснимого.  9/10, не пожалейте полчасика своей жизни и преисполнитесь космическим ужасом)

Hands-down one of the best survival games that has ever been created. Progression and narrative are absolutely fantastic and unmatched by any other game in the genre. Not to mention an absolutely gorgeous (and sometimes terrifying) world to explore.

While far from perfect, this is a definite upgrade over the first game. Significantly improved lighting, textures (on dinosaurs & environments), and & AI behavior (dinosaurs). Each dinosaur has unique social interactions and many  carnivores also have unique hunting/predation animations. Some of the downsides are that the campaign is not very long and your progress does not carry over with you. While Lagoons & Aviaries have been nice additions, they do very little to meaningfully enhance a park and are more for aesthetic purposes (Lagoons in particular). Also, there aren't really any new attractions to speak of from the first game.  It remains to be seen how much the devs will actually support JWE2 with QoL fixes. They've shipped one QoL since the game released, but I would like to see monthly updates if possible. There are still many areas the game can be improved (some of which have been addressed via mods for now).   The game is already on sale and there's almost guaranteed to be more DLC on the way. I recommend picking up on sale / in a bundle.

Marvel Snap é um jogo de cartas colecionáveis que permite aos jogadores colecionar, evoluir e batalhar com personagens icônicos do universo Marvel. O jogo é simples de jogar, mas ainda assim desafiador e altamente viciante.  O jogo apresenta uma ampla variedade de personagens da Marvel, desde heróis famosos como Homem de Ferro e Capitão América até vilões poderosos como Thanos e Ultron. Cada personagem tem habilidades e características únicas que podem ser usadas em batalha, e os jogadores podem construir sua equipe de acordo com suas preferências pessoais.  Além disso, o jogo tem uma mecânica de evolução que permite aos jogadores melhorar as habilidades e o poder de seus personagens à medida que progridem no jogo. Isso adiciona um elemento estratégico interessante, já que os jogadores precisam escolher cuidadosamente quais personagens evoluir e como gastar seus recursos limitados.  A jogabilidade de Marvel Snap é altamente viciante, com batalhas rápidas e emocionantes que mantêm os jogadores entretidos por horas a fio. O jogo também apresenta belos gráficos e efeitos sonoros, o que adiciona à imersão do jogador no universo Marvel.  Em resumo, Marvel Snap é um jogo de cartas colecionáveis altamente viciante e divertido que oferece aos jogadores uma experiência de jogo emocionante com personagens icônicos da Marvel. A mecânica de evolução adiciona um elemento estratégico interessante, e os belos gráficos e efeitos sonoros fazem com que o jogador se sinta imerso no universo Marvel.

Честно говоря, после третьей части Dark Souls мне совсем не хотелось играть в Elden Ring. С меня было достаточно быстрых врагов, кривых хитбоксов и цирка вместо пвп. И вот, запускаю я Elden Ring и… кайфую 4 часа. У нее были такие же проблемы, но об этом я узнал потом.  Плюсы: + Графика. Хочется заснять множество моментов, но часто удается заснять лишь спокойные. + Удобная карта для перемещений по открытому миру. + Смена дня и ночи не только меняет освещение, но и добавляет новых врагов. + Гибкая настройка оружия под себя. Чертовски удобно, приятный сюрприз.   Спорные моменты: (?) Музыка. Запоминающихся треков гораздо меньше, чем раньше. Амбиент разных локаций немного атмосферен, но не более. Часть песен на деле бессмысленная сгенерированная белиберда.  (?) Открытый мир напоминает ММОРПГ. Лично у меня слишком часто возникает ощущение, что в то или иное место рано идти. Персонаж просто недокачан. (?) С одной стороны хитбоксы игрока исправлены. С другой стороны, если врагу нужно ударить тебя сквозь укрытие, его ничего не остановит.  Минусы: - Управление. Прицел во врага слетает, если ДВИНУТЬ МЫШКОЙ В СТОРОНУ. СУКА, КТО БЛЯТЬ ЭТО ПРИДУМАЛ НАХУЙ. - Однообразные враги. Практически ни у одной локации нет противника, который встречался бы только там, а не где-нибудь еще. И я не про рескин уродливых птиц в красных уродливых птиц, но с другими цифрами. Чаще всего встречается или условный «миллиард бомжей» или условный «резкий как понос» одиночка. Иногда комбинированно. Середины между ними практически нет. - Из полутора сотен боссов уникальные и неповторяющиеся в лучшем случае 10 штук. Как итог первые бои интересные, а последующие быстро наскучивают. - Маления. Квинтенсенция дерьма этой игры. Она быстрая, она очень живучая, некоторые ее атаки нельзя избежать без кадров неуязвимости, она ставит отвратительный статус во второй фазе и отхиливается своими ударами, даже если они заблокированы. И даже если цель атаки мертва. - Квесты такие же «интуитивные», как и в третьей части, только теперь этот звездец в открытом мире. - Мало того что большая часть доспехов уродские(имхо), они в довесок бесполезные. Броня не качается, она слабо влияет на баланс (тот который отвечает за непрерывность атак). Тяжелая броня стыдливо курит в стороне, когда рядом появляется легкий талисман на физическое сопротивление.  - Искренне желаю тому, кто придумал залить половину мира болотами с неизлечимой красной хворью лучших благословений Дедушки Нургла.  ИТОГ: Начало игры интересное, она способна бросить тебе вызов, удивить непростым врагом, или сменой обстановки. Однако это мне быстро надоело. Бои с каждым часом становились душнее, быстрее и скучнее. Однообразные бои в однообразных локациях не были наградой. А то что выпадало в качестве награды сложно назвать чем-то еще, помимо насмешки. Середина (для меня она наступила после Штормового Замка) серьезно проседает практически во всем. Финал приносит хоть какое-то движение и интерес (для меня этот момент наступил, когда я добрался до Столицы). Честно хотелось бы поставить «палец вверх», однако я не получил того удовольствия, за которым пришел. Только духоту и геморрой.
